### Dedupe inside the serialized write, not in a pre-flight check _(proposed for this repo)_

A 'have I already added this?' check against UI state before the mutation is a race, not a guard — a double-click or a stale view appends the same thing twice. Push the dedupe into the same serialized mutator that performs the write so it sees the freshest list, and report the no-op back to the caller so the UI can say 'already there' rather than claiming success. Keep post-write reconciliation best-effort so a follow-up failure cannot fail the primary action.

### Bound every fan-out with one limiter sized by cost class _(proposed for this repo)_

A bare parallel map over N entities is an unbounded fan-out that saturates the same transport the rest of the page is waiting on, so first paint pays for a background wall. Route every per-entity fan-out through one shared concurrency limiter and set its width from the call's cost class — narrow for remote or IPC work, wider for local filesystem work, narrowest for calls that spawn real jobs. The width is a decision that belongs next to a stated reason, not a constant someone guessed.

`src/features/teams/sub_factory/passport/usePassportData.ts` defines the shared limiter and states the rule:

```ts
/** Run `fn` over `items` with at most `limit` promises in flight; results keep
 *  input order. Exported — every per-project fan-out in the factory surface
 *  should go through this instead of an unbounded Promise.all. */
export async function mapWithConcurrency<T, R>(items, limit, fn): Promise<R[]>
```

Widths are chosen per cost class, each with a stated reason:

```ts

const PROBE_FS_CONCURRENCY = 10;  // "The evidence probe is local-filesystem IPC (not remote) — wider is fine."
```

### Re-run the original pre-flight gate on every replay or rerun _(proposed for this repo)_

Replaying a recorded run is a new execution, not a playback, so it must call the identical validator the original path used. Skip it and replay silently spawns doomed work against rotated secrets, dead endpoints or a deliberately paused resource — and worse, re-fires something a human disabled on purpose. Share the validator between the two paths so 'blocked' reads identically wherever the run was started.

`src/features/triggers/sub_executions`' sibling in triggers, `src/features/triggers/hooks/useTriggerHistory.ts`, spells out the class of bug:

```ts
// signal a normal Test Fire would surface and (worst case) re-firing
// a paused trigger.

if (!validation.valid) {
  setReplayResult({ id: execution.id, success: false,
    message: failedChecks ? `Replay blocked — ${failedChecks}` : 'Replay blocked: trigger validation failed' });
  return;
}
const result = await api.executePersona(personaId, triggerId,
  execution.input_data ?? undefined, execution.use_case_id ?? undefined);
```

The validator itself is shared, not copy-pasted: `useTriggerOperations.testFire` runs the same `validateTrigger` + `failedChecks` join, so "blocked" reads identically on both paths.

### Release a dedupe mark on failure and on leaving the state _(proposed for this repo)_

Marking an id as already-notified before the notification completes is correct — it closes the duplicate-event window — but only if the mark is rolled back when that work throws, and cleared when the entity leaves the triggering state. The catch-path release is what stops one transient failure from muting the signal forever; the state-exit release is what makes the guard re-armable across the entity's lifecycle. Skipping either turns a dedupe guard into a permanent silence.

`src/features/teams/sub_assignments/useAssignmentNotificationDispatcher.ts` is the reference implementation. Duplicate `TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_PROGRESS` events are expected because "the orchestrator's tick re-entries" re-emit them, so a `Set` of already-notified ids guards the dispatch:

```ts
// Reset the dedupe key when the assignment leaves awaiting_review,
// so a future re-failure can fire another notification.
if (status !== 'awaiting_review') { notifiedRef.current.delete(assignment_id); return; }

if (notifiedRef.current.has(assignment_id)) return;
notifiedRef.current.add(assignment_id);

try {
  const detail = await getTeamAssignmentDetail(assignment_id);
  …
} catch (err) {
  // Detail fetch failures here are not fatal … Undo the dedupe mark so a
  // subsequent awaiting_review event for this assignment retries the
  // notification instead of being permanently suppressed.
  notifiedRef.current.delete(assignment_id);
  silentCatch('teams/useAssignmentNotificationDispatcher')(err);
}
```

Both releases matter for different reasons: the transition release makes the guard *re-armable* across the entity's lifecycle; the catch release makes it *not a permanent mute* after one flak

### Poll short calls for long work, with a cap and a cancel check _(proposed for this repo)_

Holding one request open for minutes of backend work turns the client timeout into an at-least-once hazard and leaks the call when the view unmounts. Spawn the work, take a fast handle back, and poll with short calls in a loop that has an explicit iteration cap, checks a mounted or cancel ref before every await and before every commit, and exposes a user-facing stop. The cap bounds the pathological case; the ref is what stops the loop from running for twenty minutes after the user navigated away.

`src/features/teams/sub_deliberations/useTeamDeliberations.ts`:

```ts

// poll-reap until its output posts, then advance one recovery round …
let d = await approveDeliberationAction(id);
…
// Wait out the capability (each poll is a short call — no long invoke).
for (let i = 0; i < 600 && mountedRef.current && d.status === 'action_running'; i++) {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000));
  d = await pollDeliberationAction(id);
}
if (!mountedRef.current) return;
```

The cancellation refs and why they exist:

```ts
// Cooperative cancellation for the long-running loops. Without this,
// approveAction's reap loop kept polling every 2s for up to 20 minutes
// after the user navigated away (plus the post-loop refresh fan-out), and
// runToBudget/runAllTracks only stopped on teamId change, not on unmount.
const mountedRef = useRef(true);
useEffect(() => { mountedRef.current = true;
  return () => { mountedRef.current = false; runningRef.current = false; }; }, []);
```

### Supersede stale responses with a request token, not a boolean _(proposed for this repo)_

A boolean 'already fetching' guard cannot tell a duplicate poll (drop it) from a new request after a filter change (must run), and it does nothing about out-of-order responses. Bump a monotonic counter per call and let only the response whose sequence still matches write to state, so overlapping requests are allowed and the newest one wins. Close and cancel must bump the counter too, or an in-flight fetch writes into a panel the user already dismissed.

### Latch one attempt per session for self-scheduled jobs _(proposed for this repo)_

'Run this periodically on launch' jobs fail in two independent ways. Returning on a transient failure without latching lets every re-render of the host re-fire the effect into a tight retry storm, so make one attempt per session the contract regardless of outcome. And a corrupt stored timestamp makes the elapsed-time comparison always false, so the job runs on every launch — treat any unparseable timestamp as 'never run' so the next success rewrites a valid one.

`src/features/agents/sub_health/useHealthDigestScheduler.ts`:

```ts
function parseLastRunMs(raw: string | null | undefined): number | null {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string' || raw.length === 0) return null;
  const ms = new Date(raw).getTime();
  return Number.isFinite(ms) ? ms : null;
}
```
> "Guard against corrupt/legacy timestamp values: treat any non-ISO or unparseable string as 'never run' so we run once and immediately rewrite a valid ISO stamp, instead of spamming the digest on every launch when `now - NaN` is always false."

```ts

  // Attempt failed (transient). Previously we returned without latching
  // ran.current and the finally below released running.current — every
  // subsequent re-render of the host component re-fired the effect,
  // hammering the IPC layer in a tight retry storm. Treat one attempt
  // per app session as the contract...
  ran.current = true;
  return;
}
```
The cleanup path is Strict-Mode aware: `if (!ran.current) running.current = false;` in both the `finally` and the unmount, so the second dev mount can still run.

### Cancel by advancing a generation counter, never by resetting a flag _(proposed for this repo)_

A boolean 'cancelled' flag that any later scheduler resets can revive work the user already stopped, because the pending task re-reads the flag after the reset. Key a monotonic counter per logical stream, have each scheduled task capture the value it was born with, and abort as soon as its key's value differs. Key by the finest independent stream — cancelling in one conversation or terminal must not stop a pending task in another.

`src-tauri/src/companion/session.rs:178-231` replaced a single `AtomicBool` after a live bug:

> This replaces a single `AtomicBool` that was *reset* on every new schedule: a user "stop" set the bool, but if that same turn's reply also emitted `continue_autonomously`, `schedule_autonomous_tick` reset the bool and the originally-pending tick — still polling — saw `cancelled == false` and fired, so the loop the user halted kept running (bug-hunt 2026-06-07 companion #1).

The fix is `static AUTONOMOUS_GENS: Mutex<Option<HashMap<String, u64>>>` with `autonomy_gen_of()` / `cancel_pending_autonomy()` / `autonomous_superseded()`. Keying by conversation was a second fix on the same axis: a stop in thread A must not cancel a pending tick in thread B. The tick polls `autonomous_superseded()` every 200ms during its 15s delay and again at the delay boundary (`session.rs:1220-1240`).

The same shape recurs in the frontend for a different reason — `fleetTerminalManager.ts:434-458` uses `const gen = ++m.hydrationGen` so a superseded terminal snapshot is dropped rather than written over live output, and `drive/hooks/useDrive.ts:355-370` uses `recursiveSearchSeq` because `driveSearch` is 'as

_(evidence truncated)_

### Put every concurrent dimension into an out-of-process job's dedup key _(proposed for this repo)_

For work that runs in a process you do not control, three decisions carry the design. The dedup key must include every dimension that is meant to run concurrently, or parallel work collides as duplicates of itself. 'Finished' is a transition out of the active states you can observe by polling — for an interactive session that is idle, not exited — so make the result import idempotent with an on-disk marker and it is safe to fire on any settle signal.

`src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_workspaces/practiceHarvestPrompt.ts:29-39`:

> Fleet dedup key for a per-scope harvest session. The scope is part of the key: several territories of the same repo are meant to run concurrently, and a repo-level key would make them collide as duplicates of each other.

`.../sub_workspaces/useHarvestAutoIngest.ts:4-10` records the live-test finding that fixed the edge detection:

> "Ends" means settling out of the active states — for an interactive CLI session that is `idle` (the prompt), NOT `exited`: a finished session sits idle forever (live-test finding, 2026-07-23). Ingest is idempotent (the run-dir `ingested.json` marker), so firing on idle/exit/vanish after an active phase is safe.

Two double-fire guards sit on top: an `ingesting = useRef<Set<string>>` in-flight set, and a `markLive()` armed at dispatch time "so a fast-settling wave still produces a running→gone transition even if the first poll misses it" (`:54-61`). A run-dir name replaces `:` with `-` because "a colon is not a legal path character on Windows".

## data

### Derive the value instead of storing a copy that can drift _(proposed for this repo)_

A stored duplicate of something computable drifts the moment one writer forgets to update it, and the drift is silent. Prefer a pure derived function, and treat not-known as a modelled state rather than a fabricated zero. Cache or store only when the derive is measurably hot, and then own the invalidation explicitly rather than hoping.

**Practiced here:**
- Connector readiness is a pure derived function, not a stored enum — agents/connectors
- "null is a first-class answer" — passport & scene render an explicit em-dash, never invent data — passportDerive.ts · deriveScene.ts
- Draft/baseline diffing keyed by field-group arrays with a compile-time exhaustiveness guard — agents/PersonaDraft.ts

**Limits — when NOT to apply**

Derivation costs CPU on every read: cache or store when the derive is hot and provably expensive, but then own the invalidation explicitly. "Model unknown" is not a licence to render nothing — an em-dash still needs an explanation path.

---
*Evidence counts are synthesis estimates over the 159-finding scan corpus (16 agents, two waves), not exact joins. Full per-finding evidence lives in the scan corpus; the divergences below carry verified file:line.*

### Keep every SQL statement behind a repository module _(proposed for this repo)_

When one subsystem declares its schema inline and issues raw queries straight from command handlers, the data layer stops having a single edge — nobody can find, test or migrate that table with the tooling that covers the rest. Route every statement through a repository module even when the subsystem's storage model is deliberately unusual; the storage choice and the boundary are two separate decisions.

Violates **Enforce module boundaries and layering** (doctrine D4).

**Evidence**

`db/mod.rs:635-1117` defines the whole `COMPANION_SCHEMA` inline as a SQL constant (no migration file, no repo module); query code sits in `commands/companion/brain.rs:296,418-423,431` as raw `conn.prepare`. **Note:** the companion's markdown-as-source-of-truth inversion is documented and deliberate (`companion/mod.rs:6-9`) — the divergence is the missing repo boundary, not the storage model.

### Give every list query a default bound, no exceptions _(proposed for this repo)_

One unbounded list query among bounded siblings stays invisible until the table grows: it reads and serialises every row on a path that was sized for a page, and nothing in review flags it because the code looks like its neighbours. Make a default limit part of the repository's contract, so an unbounded read has to be asked for explicitly.

Violates **Bounded, self-instrumenting, reliable-by-construction pipelines** (doctrine D6).

**Evidence**

`db/repos` — `personas::get_all` returns every row with no LIMIT, while sibling repos default to 50-200.

### Store money as integer minor units and convert at one seam _(proposed for this repo)_

Float currency accumulates error the moment the database aggregates it, and conversions scattered across callers guarantee that at least one of them rounds differently. Let the store speak integer minor units so aggregation is exact, and put the conversion to and from display units at exactly one boundary module — the same move applies to any heuristic score crossing into a fixed-precision ledger.

`src/lib/data/transactions-db.ts:26-31,57,263`: "this store speaks integer CENTS (amount_cents bigint) so SQL can never [accumulate float error]", "Float dollars → integer cents. Math.round kills the classic 184.22*100 = ..." issue; `amount: Number(row.amount_cents) / 100` on read, `revenue[idx] = Number(row.revenue_cents) / 100; // cents → dollars; buildMonthlySeries re-rounds to cents.` CLAUDE.md codifies this: "Money: boundary speaks float dollars; the store speaks integer cents; conversion only at transactions-db.ts." A whole `src/lib/money/` module (arithmetic.ts, round-to-cents.ts, parse-money.ts, allocate.ts, format.ts) backs this with ADRs 0001-0009.

### Commit to one SQL dialect so drivers never fork the query strings _(proposed for this repo)_

Supporting several database drivers tempts you to branch SQL per environment, and those branches drift until only one of them is really tested. Pick a single dialect every driver honours, resolve the driver once per process behind a cached accessor, and dynamically import each driver so unused ones never enter the bundle. Return a reason when nothing resolves — an opaque null is undiagnosable.

`src/lib/db/index.ts:1-15`: "Every consumer goes through getDb(); SQL strings stay IDENTICAL across drivers because all three are real Postgres." `ResolveDriverResult` is a discriminated union carrying a human-readable `reason` on null (lines 44-49) instead of an opaque null — "a typo'd DB_DRIVER, or nothing configured" is diagnosable. Cache invariant documented explicitly at lines 89-99: cache is keyed only on driver name, connection env is captured at construction, so a rotated `DATABASE_URL` is NOT picked up without a restart — a named, accepted limitation.

### Register every feature's storage through one shared store factory _(proposed for this repo)_

Per-feature bespoke stores duplicate tenant scoping and each invents its own concurrency story. Define one factory that hands a feature a typed CRUD store, tenant-scoped on every call and backed by a real driver or an in-memory dev fallback — and give it atomic create-if-absent and compare-and-set primitives, so ledgers and state machines do not have to grow their own.

src/lib/db/feature-store.ts:14-16 describes the driver switch; :23-58 defines `create()` (atomic, detects id collision so a chain-of-custody ledger append can't silently overwrite under a race) and `swap()` (compare-and-set for e.g. an artifact's signed→delivered flip, preventing double-charge under concurrent callers). ADR-0007/ADR-0008 in docs/adr/ trace the evolution from a bespoke per-feature `Map<tenantId, Map<id,T>>` (still described in CULTURE.md's 'Repository pattern' section) to this shared adapter — matters/store.ts and counter-offer-store.ts both consume it identically.

### Consolidate every connection into one pool with one tuning point _(proposed for this repo)_

Modules that each open their own connection pool drift in exactly the settings that matter — pool size, TLS, statement timeout, schema sanitising — and the drift stays invisible until one of them misbehaves under load. Put the pool behind a single accessor that returns nothing when unconfigured, and let alternate embedded drivers implement the same interface rather than forking the callers.

`src/lib/db/pool.ts:1-24` documents the consolidation explicitly: five modules used to each declare their own `global.__xPool` + `pool()` factory and their own `AUTH_SCHEMA` sanitiser, and had already drifted (`polar` used `max: 2` while others used `max: 3`). The comment: "They all live here now: one pool, one schema name, one place to tune SSL / max / statement_timeout." `getPool()` returns `null` when unconfigured (keyless demo mode), and a swappable `DB_DRIVER=pglite` adapter (`src/lib/db/pglite-pool.ts`) implements the same `DbPool` interface backed by an embedded WASM Postgres for local dev, with a FIFO mutex documented at pglite-pool.ts:20-26 to serialize transactions on the single embedded connection.

### Make the client/server storage split a stated rule, not a precedent _(proposed for this repo)_

When some data lives in browser storage and some in a server database, the boundary is a real architectural decision — but if it is only visible as precedent, every new module re-decides it by imitation and the split slowly stops meaning anything. Name the classes of data each store owns and where the line falls, so the choice is looked up rather than guessed.

- `src/lib/contacts/store.ts`, `src/lib/settings/store.ts`, `src/lib/recurring/store.ts`, `src/lib/invoice/archive.ts`, `src/lib/invoice/drafts.ts`, `src/lib/invoice/numbering.ts` all call `localStorage.getItem/setItem` directly.
- `src/lib/db/connection.ts:8-20` — module-level singleton `let db: Database.Database | null` opened lazily with WAL + foreign_keys pragmas, used only from `src/app/api/tax/**/route.ts`.
- No repo-level abstraction unifies the two; a dev adding a new module must decide localStorage-vs-sqlite themselves based on precedent, not a documented rule.

### Migrate stored settings forward, then deep-merge over defaults _(proposed for this repo)_

A version-keyed migration chain handles shape changes, but it cannot know about fields added after it was written. Wrap the payload as version plus data, run the chain forward, then merge the result over freshly-built defaults so any key no migration ever wrote backfills instead of crashing. Detect legacy unwrapped payloads by shape rather than assuming version zero.

`src/lib/settings/store.ts:31-78` — `runMigrations` walks `fromVersion..SETTINGS_VERSION`, then `mergeDeep(createDefaultSettings(), migrated)`. Comment at line 33-36 explains the deliberate policy: 'No structural rewrite is required today because deep-merge with defaults backfills missing keys; future shape changes ... go here.' Legacy unwrapped v0 payloads are detected via `readStored` (line 46-57) checking for the `{version, data}` shape.

### Track applied migrations in a table and make the run idempotent _(proposed for this repo)_

If the apply loop reads a set of already-applied versions and skips them, running migrations becomes safe on every request rather than a startup-only ritual — which removes a whole class of ordering bugs in serverless and hot-reload environments. A migration may repair data as well as change schema: clean the existing bad rows and add the constraint that prevents recurrence in the same step.

`src/lib/db/migrate.ts:9-213` — four migrations including a data-fixing migration (v4, `gdpr_consents_dedupe`, lines 187-212) that both cleans existing duplicate rows via a window-function DELETE and adds a partial UNIQUE INDEX to prevent recurrence — an example of migration-as-both-schema-and-data-repair. `runMigrations()` (215-242) creates `_migrations` if missing, then only executes migrations whose version isn't in the applied set. Route handlers call `ensureDb()` which wraps `runMigrations(); return getDb();` per-request (see `src/app/api/tax/submit/route.ts:8-11`) rather than running migrations once at startup.

### Leave unknown values unknown and report the gap to the user _(proposed for this repo)_

Interpolating a missing timestamp or estimating an unresolved price makes a dataset look complete while quietly corrupting every aggregate computed from it. Keep the unknown sentinel through ingestion and analysis, and surface the gap in plain language in the UI, so the reader knows what was not answered instead of trusting a fabricated number.

`lib/chain.ts:161-164` docstring: 'We never interpolate a timestamp — an unknown ts is left 0, never faked.' `lib/swapingest.ts:22-27` docstring: 'USD price is written only when the quote side is a stablecoin, else it is left unknown (0) rather than faked.' `lib/scan.ts:189` surfaces to the user: 'Retry, or check DUNE_API_KEY / credits. No wallets fabricated.' `app/components/pipeline.tsx:49-51` renders that same invariant back into the UI ('The token library below is real; wallets fill on retry. No wallets are fabricated.'). This is a cross-cutting integrity doctrine, not a one-off comment.

### Compose the store interface from narrow per-domain repositories _(proposed for this repo)_

One flat persistence interface becomes a place any feature can reach any other feature's data. Compose it from narrow per-domain repository interfaces and have each feature narrow the shared accessor down to its own, so a cross-domain call fails at compile time. Cache the in-flight promise rather than the resolved value, or two concurrent cold starts each build their own database.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:1-20` states the rule directly: "Auth, the token ledger, and EVERY domain feature storage module talk ONLY to this `Store` interface ... the concrete driver ... is chosen by `@/lib/db/config` and loaded lazily here so neither module enters the bundle unless it's used." The interface is composed at `store.ts:704-724` (`interface Store extends ProfileRepository, TokenRepository, GrantRepository, ...`). `getStore()` (`store.ts:729-749`) caches the *promise* (not the resolved value) assigned synchronously before any `await`, explicitly to avoid a double cold-start race that would run `CORE_DDL` twice — a documented concurrency-correctness fix baked into the chokepoint itself. Feature storage modules (e.g. `src/features/drafts/storage.ts:23-27`) each narrow `getStore()`'s return type down to their own repository interface (`DraftRepository`) via a small `getDraftRepository()` wrapper, so a stray cross-domain call from inside a feature module is a compile-time error.

### Merge partial updates in the database, never read-modify-write _(proposed for this repo)_

When several writers touch different parts of one document — autosave, an assistant suggestion, a second tab — an application-layer read-modify-write clobbers whichever sibling was written in between. Express the update as a single database-level merge of the partial input and implement it natively per driver. State it at the interface, because the wrong layer is exactly where the pre-read creeps back in.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:324-336` (DraftRepository.updateDraftSections): "MUST be a single atomic DB merge, NOT a read-modify-write — concurrent autosave / AI-suggest / multi-tab writes rely on the DB merging so one write can't clobber a section another just saved." Mirrored at `store.ts:408-419` for reports. The feature layer (`src/features/drafts/storage.ts:60-81`, `upsertDraftSections`) explicitly documents that its own pre-read of `existing` is only an existence gate, "NOT the merge basis any more" — a comment added specifically to prevent a future edit from reintroducing read-modify-write at the wrong layer.

### Select the persistence driver lazily behind one cached accessor _(proposed for this repo)_

Choosing a backend by config only pays off if call sites never see the choice. Resolve the driver inside a single accessor that dynamic-imports it, caches the in-flight promise so concurrent cold starts share one instance, clears the cache on rejection so a transient import failure can retry, and wraps the resolved driver with cross-cutting concerns once on behalf of every driver author.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:1-11` docstring states the boundary explicitly. `getStore()` (lines 385-418) caches the in-flight PROMISE (not the resolved value) to prevent two concurrent cold-start callers from building divergent PGlite in-memory databases, clears the cache on rejection so a transient import failure can retry, and wraps the resolved driver with `withDomainEvents` (event bus) before returning — so every driver gets domain-event publishing for free without each driver author remembering to call it.

### Soft-delete evidence rows and append rather than edit consent _(proposed for this repo)_

For records that may later be disputed — filed evidence, consent, chain of custody — an in-place update destroys the very history the record exists to prove. Soft-delete instead, keeping the row and its never-reused ordinal recoverable, and make a changed preference a new row rather than an edit. Conditional mutations should report whether a live row matched instead of throwing on a no-op.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:361-382` (`removeCaseDocument`/`restoreCaseDocument`/`refileCaseDocument` docstrings) and lines 36-47 (`RecordConsentInput` docstring: 'Append-only consent/preference record (no profile mutation)'). Both mutation methods return `boolean` for 'did a LIVE row match' rather than throwing on no-op, which the adapter layer's `wrapFound` helper (result.ts:56-68) turns into a `not_found` AdapterResult rather than a false success.

### Apply status changes conditionally on the status you expect _(proposed for this repo)_

A status update that does not name the states it may apply from lets a double-submit or a stale tab perform an illegal transition. Make the allowed source states part of the write, bundle any append-only log entries into the same operation so the log cannot drift from the status, and return whether it applied rather than throwing when a legitimate race loses.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:169-187, 320-327`. The same 'boolean = did it actually apply, not a thrown exception' shape recurs across all conditional mutations in this Store (transitionCase, removeCaseDocument, restoreCaseDocument, refileCaseDocument) — a consistent, deliberate convention rather than one-off.

### Enforce the persistence boundary in the linter, then test the rule _(proposed for this repo)_

A documented boundary that lives only in a README is re-crossed the first time somebody imports the driver directly. Encode it as import-restriction zones — app code cannot reach a driver, persistence cannot reach auth — make every message cite the decision record so a blocked developer lands on the reasoning, and assert the rule's exact behaviour by running the real config against virtual file paths in a test.

- `src/lib/db/store.ts:1-16` doc comment: "Auth ... the token ledger ... and EVERY domain module talk ONLY to this `Store` interface; the concrete driver (Firestore in prod, PGlite locally) is chosen by `@/lib/db/config` and loaded lazily here."
- `eslint.config.mjs:70-146` defines two non-overlapping `no-restricted-imports` zones (app+domain vs. persistence) each citing "ADR-0013" in the error message.
- `src/lib/boundaries.test.ts:1-136` — drives the real flat config via `new ESLint({cwd: root})` and `lintText({filePath})`, asserting e.g. `assertBlocked(APP, 'import { Client } from "pg"')` and `assertAllowed(STORE, 'import { Client } from "pg"')`, with every blocked case required to cite ADR-0013 in its message so reviewers land on the doc.
- The Store interface itself documents driver-swap extensibility: "To add a backend, implement `Store` and wire it into `getStore()` — no call-site changes."

### Say so at the interface when two backends model a concept differently _(proposed for this repo)_

Behind one storage interface, drivers sometimes need genuinely different shapes — a relational child table on one side, an embedded array on the other. That is legitimate, but a reader who assumes a one-to-one mapping will extend only one side and ship a silent asymmetry. Document the divergence at the interface and keep a parity test, because nothing else forces both implementations to satisfy the same contract.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:669-681` — full comment block: "The two backends INTENTIONALLY model this differently and share no mapping logic ... do NOT assume a 1:1 collection↔table name mapping. Both honor the contract below." This is flagged as a pattern worth knowing (not a bug) but the ftype note: any NEW Store method must independently verify both driver implementations satisfy the same contract since there's no shared adapter enforcing shape parity beyond `schema-parity.test.ts`.

### Never cache a 'no driver configured' result — let late config heal _(proposed for this repo)_

Memoising the resolved persistence driver is right; memoising the absence of one is not. If configuration arrives after the first call — a secret injected late, an env var set by a supervisor — a cached null disables persistence for the whole process lifetime with no way back. Cache the resolved driver only, and re-resolve on absence.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:1-10,415-435`: header comment states the doctrine explicitly — auth and ledger code talk ONLY to `Store`; adding a backend means implementing the interface and wiring `getStore()`, with zero call-site changes. `getStore()` memoizes a resolved driver but deliberately does NOT cache a `null` (no driver configured) result, so late env injection (e.g. `DATABASE_URL` arriving after first call) can self-heal instead of permanently disabling persistence for the process lifetime (comment at line 415-418).

### Assign the store promise before the first await, not after it _(proposed for this repo)_

A lazy async accessor that awaits before assigning its cache lets two concurrent first callers both open the backend — fatal when the backend is a single-connection embedded database. Assign the promise synchronously and let both await the shared handle. Keep the composition itself thin: one file per repository, assembled by spreading them into one object.

`lib/db/store.ts:1-45` doc comment: "Every consumer... talks ONLY to this `Store` interface... To add a backend: implement `Store`, wire it into `getStore()`. No call-site changes." The cache-before-await pattern at lines 192-204: `cached = (async () => {...})();` is assigned synchronously before the internal await, specifically to avoid a race on PGlite's single-connection constraint. `lib/db/pglite-store.ts` is a thin composer: `return { ...makeGraphRepo(pg), ...makeVoteRepo(pg), ... }` — each repository lives in its own file under `lib/db/pglite/repositories/`.

### Separate incremental batches from full-snapshot syncs at the API _(proposed for this repo)_

A batch that is the complete current state of a dataset carries information a partial batch does not: whatever is absent has disappeared. Give the two cases different entry points so disappearance becomes a first-class detected signal instead of stale rows lingering forever, and make each caller state which kind of source it has rather than inferring it.

`crates/core/src/app.rs:356-373` — `sync_many` doc: "Use instead of upsert_many when items is the complete current state of the dataset ... the summary's removed keys are the disappeared-record signal (delisted grants, closed vacancies, removed listings)". `crates/apps/hackernews/src/lib.rs:80-82` demonstrates the choice explicitly in a comment: "The front page is a full snapshot, so use sync_many: a story that has dropped off is marked removed rather than lingering forever."

### Put all persistence behind one store interface and a lazy driver _(proposed for this repo)_

Six independent projects in this workspace converged on the same arrangement: a single store interface composed from per-domain repositories, with the concrete driver chosen by config and dynamically imported inside a cached accessor. Adding a backend then means implementing the interface and nothing else — no call-site changes, and no unused driver in the bundle.

**Independently converged on by 6 projects**

- Grant Writing Nonprofits
- Immigration Paperwork
- Local SEO Agency
- Medical Bill Negotiator
- politicas
- ai-bookkeeper

A pattern this many projects reached independently is a candidate workspace-wide standard.

### Preview a cascading change, but let the backend decide the reconcile _(proposed for this repo)_

Before an edit that silently breaks other records, query the affected counts and require confirmation — and show no dialog at all when nothing is affected. Keep that preview strictly advisory: it is debounced and may still be in flight at save time, so gating the actual reconcile call on it lets a fast save skip rewiring consumers. The backend is authoritative and reports zero when there was nothing to do.

`src/features/agents/sub_use_cases/libs/useCapabilityToggle.ts` splits the paths by risk: activation applies immediately ("the cascade is always safe on activation"), while deactivation first calls `getUseCaseCascade()` and only opens the confirm dialog when triggers/subscriptions/automations are actually affected — no dialog for a no-op. The success toast reports what cascaded (`Paused capability (cascaded: 2 triggers, 1 subscription)`).

`src/features/agents/sub_use_cases/components/core/EventRenameModal.tsx` offers three explicit consumer actions (update / delete / leave — "they'll silently stop receiving the event"), debounces the counting IPC by 300ms (it "used to fire countEventListeners (an SQLite-scanning IPC) for BOTH columns of every non-empty row per keystroke (~2N queries per key)"), and discards late responses per row by comparing queried text to current text. Then, on save:

> "We deliberately do NOT pre-filter on `existingCounts` here: those counts are a best-effort advisory fetch (debounced, may still be in flight when the user hits Save) and gating the reconcile call on them means a fast save can silently skip rewiring consumers."

### Autosave by diffing a small derived slice, debounced, flushed on exit _(proposed for this repo)_

Persisting a long flow directly from its in-memory state writes constantly and writes stale snapshots. Derive a small persistence slice, skip the write when it equals the last synced one, debounce it, re-read the freshest state at write time rather than closing over a snapshot, and flush on unmount so closing a modal never loses the last edit. The in-memory reducer stays the single source of truth.

`src/features/templates/sub_n8n/hooks/useN8nSession.ts` syncs one reducer to two sinks (SQLite via Tauri at 600ms, localStorage at 300ms):

```ts
function deriveDbSlice(state): DbSlice { step, status: deriveSessionStatus(state), parserResult: cachedStringify(…), … }
if (lastSyncedSliceRef.current && slicesEqual(lastSyncedSliceRef.current, currentSlice)) return;
dbTimerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
  // Read the freshest state at write time to avoid syncing a stale snapshot
  const freshSlice = deriveDbSlice(latestStateRef.current);
  …
}, DB_SYNC_DELAY);
```

The status column is *derived*, not stored (`deriveSessionStatus` maps reducer flags to the `SessionStatus` union), which keeps the persisted row from drifting from what the UI shows. The effect's dependency list is hand-written per field with the reason attached: "the whole `state` object is deliberately NOT a dep so per-line stream dispatches (TRANSFORM_LINES etc.) don't re-run this effect." An unmount effect clears both timers and performs the pending write immediately so a modal close never loses the last edit.

The restore side is guarded rather than trusted — `handleSessionLoaded` re-validates the persisted st

_(evidence truncated)_

### Refuse to save a config whose load failed _(proposed for this repo)_

A panel that falls back to empty defaults when loading fails will, on the next save, persist those defaults over the real stored config. Track load success separately from data presence and block the write until a successful reload, keeping a parse failure as first-class UI state rather than collapsing it into 'nothing configured'. When the config is a security policy, this is a security regression rather than an inconvenience.

`src/features/settings/sub_byom/libs/useByomSettings.ts` states the failure mode and the fix in code:

```ts
// Refuse to save when the initial load failed (corrupt JSON OR a transient IPC
// error). Without this gate, the in-memory `policy` is `defaultPolicy()` — empty
// allow-lists, no routing/compliance rules — and saving it would silently
// overwrite the on-disk policy. BYOM controls which providers see persona
// secrets, so a policy wipe is a security regression.
if (!loaded || corruptPolicyError !== null) { addToast('Cannot save: ...', 'error'); return; }
```

The hook also keeps `corruptPolicyError` as first-class UI state rather than collapsing a parse failure into "no policy", and re-snapshots dirty-state from the object it actually persisted (`savedSnapshotRef.current = snapshot`) instead of from live state, so a concurrent edit can't make a saved policy look clean.

### Anchor time buckets on the data's own dates, not the client clock _(proposed for this repo)_

Deriving the current period from the local clock mislabels the head bucket whenever the client sits on the other side of the boundary from whatever bucketed the data. Anchor on the maximum date present in the returned series and do the arithmetic in UTC. The same discipline clamps negative age differences, so a future-dated row cannot slip past a max-age window.

`src/features/settings/sub_limits/components/LimitsSettings.tsx`:

```ts
// Anchor "current month" on the server's own bucketed date domain (the max
// chart_points date) rather than the client's local clock — a client behind/ahead
// of the server around a month boundary would otherwise mislabel the head row.
const maxKey = data.chart_points.reduce((acc, pt) => {
  const key = pt.date.slice(0, 7);
  return !acc || key > acc ? key : acc;
}, null);
const anchor = maxKey ? new Date(`${maxKey}-01T00:00:00Z`) : new Date();
const d = new Date(Date.UTC(anchor.getUTCFullYear(), anchor.getUTCMonth() - i, 1));
```

The same clock-skew discipline shows up in `src/features/home/sub_welcome/useResumeContext.ts`, which clamps negative age diffs (`Math.max(0, now - ts)`) so a future-dated `created_at` can't slip past a max-age window, and sorts explicitly by timestamp rather than trusting array order.

### Recompute dependents on every write, and resolve them before a delete _(proposed for this repo)_

When another record's runnability depends on a shared row — a credential, a config, a licence — every create, edit and delete must recompute those dependents' derived readiness in the same command, or a run gate that should have blocked lets work execute against a dead reference. For deletes, resolve the dependent set first: the scan usually reads a column that vanishes with the row.

`src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/crud.rs::delete_credential`:
```rust
// Capture the affected persona set BEFORE the row is gone — the dependents
// scan reads the credential's `service_type`, which vanishes on delete.
let affected = connector_readiness::credential_dependent_persona_ids(&state.db, &id);
let result = repo::delete(&state.db, &id)?;
if result {
    // Deleting a bound credential leaves any persona linked to it with a
    // dead `credentialLinks` id — recompute so `setup_status` flips to
    // `needs_credentials` and the run gate blocks instead of executing blind.
    for pid in &affected { connector_readiness::recompute_persona_setup(&state.db, pid) ... }
}
```
The same recompute fires on `update_credential` and on `update_credential_field`, gated on whether field data actually changed: *"Editing field values can turn a usable credential into an empty / stale one (or vice versa) — recompute readiness for personas bound to it so `setup_status` stays honest."*

User-facing counterpart: before the delete confirm, `CredentialDeleteDialog.tsx` fetches `credential_blast_radius` and renders the affected agents inside the destructive-confirm modal. The graph behind

### Version every persisted document and sanitise it on read _(proposed for this repo)_

Anything persisted outlives the validation that wrote it: historical rows already hold values your current input rules would reject. Give the document a version, store machine tokens rather than rendered labels so it stays language-agnostic, and read it through a tolerant parser that coerces each field to its expected shape and degrades unrecognised values instead of throwing.

**Tokens, not labels** — `src/features/triggers/sub_studio/libs/studioDraftModel.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Run-condition gating a link. Stored as a token (never a display string) so
 * the persisted draft stays language-agnostic; labels resolve via i18n at
 * render time. null = always run.
 */
export type LinkCondition = 'on_success' | 'on_failure' | 'output_match' | null;
```

**Tolerant read with degradation** — same file:

```ts
if (parsed.version === 1 && Array.isArray(parsed.links)) {
  // Round-1 prototype drafts stored display strings as conditions;
  // anything that isn't a known token degrades to "always".
  for (const link of parsed.links) {
    if (!LINK_CONDITION_PRESETS.includes(link.condition)) link.condition = null;
  }
  return parsed;
}
```

`src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts::parseLayout` does the field-by-field version: "Parse a serialized layout doc, coercing each field to its expected shape and falling back to empty on malformed / non-object input (never throws)." `parseDataLinkIds` in `usePassportData.ts` is the same idea for a JSON column: "Tolerant — malformed content reads as no links, never a crash."

## errors

### Tell 'not configured' apart from a real outage before logging _(proposed for this repo)_

A provider that collapses every failure to a uniform empty value gives the caller a clean contract and gives the operator nothing — a genuine outage then looks exactly like an unconfigured build. Keep the uniform return, but add a separate telemetry seam that records why the call failed, staying silent only for the reasons you expect and recording every other reason with structured context.

`src/lib/ai/telemetry.ts:1-13`: "a genuine outage was therefore invisible: success theater. recordAiFailure restores the distinction." `AiFailureReason` union enumerates 8 named reasons including domain-specific ones (`rejected-direction`, `unknown-account` for categorize; `ungrounded-number` for concierge/insights). `console.error` calls are explicitly marked as a placeholder seam: "a real telemetry sink (metrics counter, error tracker) can replace them later without touching the providers."

### Return a result at every domain boundary; throw only for bugs _(proposed for this repo)_

Reserve thrown exceptions for programmer error and genuinely exceptional conditions; anything a caller could reasonably handle should come back as a two-variant result carrying the error in the type system. The point is not ceremony — a thrown error crossing a module boundary loses its variants, so an exhaustive switch over the failure modes stops being verifiable.

src/lib/result.ts:1-19 defines `ok`/`err`/`isOk`/`isErr`. docs/CULTURE.md 'Earned conventions' section: 'thrown errors crossing module boundaries lose their type info; Result<T,E> keeps the error variants in the type system so an exhaustive switch is verifiable... When to use string-thrown errors instead: truly exceptional conditions... If a caller might reasonably handle the error, use Result. If they should crash, throw.' callAI.ts consistently returns `Result<AIResponse, AICallError>` (never throws) across 5 distinct error branches (missing_api_key, cost_ceiling_exceeded, model_error, empty_response, quality_blocked, multimodal_unsupported).

### Flatten results into a reason union before crossing the network _(proposed for this repo)_

A result type designed for in-process use serializes awkwardly across a server/client network boundary, and a thrown server action becomes an opaque network error on the client. Return a flat discriminated union whose variants are string-literal reasons, and map reasons to copy in one function per feature so the client never parses a message.

docs/CULTURE.md 'Server actions return discriminated-union Results': example `DraftDemandLetterResult = {ok:true; artifactId; citesVerified; costUsd} | {ok:false; reason:"matter_not_found"} | {ok:false; reason:"missing_api_key"} | {ok:false; reason:"cite_verification_failed"; failedCites} | {ok:false; reason:"model_error"; message}`. `src/features/matters/actions.ts` defines `CreateMatterResult` in the same shape. Rationale given: 'server-action throws turn into opaque network errors on the client.'

### Let transient provider failures escape the degradation path _(proposed for this repo)_

Routes that degrade to a deterministic heuristic on any provider failure return success and hide real outages. Give transient failures — rate limits, provider errors, timeouts — a distinct error type so they can escape the degradation path and surface as an actionable status, while content failures such as unparseable model output keep degrading silently. Classify defensively: anything not clearly transient stays on the fallback path.

`src/lib/llm/errors.ts:1-15` states the problem directly: metered routes degrade to a deterministic heuristic on ANY provider failure and return 200 — which silently hides a real outage. `classifyLlmError()` (errors.ts:43-55) defensively classifies raw provider errors by numeric status (429, 500/502/503/504) or `TimeoutError` name (from an `AbortSignal.timeout()` abort), returning `null` for anything not clearly transient so the caller's heuristic fallback still applies to content failures. The module deliberately has no `server-only` import so the pure classification logic can be unit tested and imported by both server-only providers and (implicitly) any future client code.

### Return a typed store error for writes, and preflight the quota _(proposed for this repo)_

Storage writes fail in ways the caller must handle — quota exhaustion, a disabled store — and they fail differently in each browser. Return a discriminated store error with a small kind union instead of throwing, classify quota across the vendors' divergent error names, and preflight the payload size so the common failure is refused before the write is attempted at all.

`src/lib/contacts/store.ts:16-27` defines `StoreError` + `isStoreError`; `classifyWriteError` (29-51) special-cases `QuotaExceededError`/`NS_ERROR_DOM_QUOTA_REACHED` and falls back to message-sniffing. `preflightSize` (53-61) rejects oversized payloads before ever touching `localStorage.setItem`. `saveContact`/`updateContact` (150-213) return `Contact | StoreError` union types. Same `ExportResult` discriminated-union shape appears in `src/lib/feedback/result.ts:1-3` (`{ok:true,...} | {ok:false, reason}`), showing the result-object-over-exception convention is repo-wide, not local to one file.

### Give every API route the same error envelope and status map _(proposed for this repo)_

Every route that touches an external service or a database needs the same envelope: validate inputs before the risky call, choose the status from the cause, and wrap the call so an unexpected throw still leaves through the envelope. The shape is only worth anything if it is universal — one handler that skips the wrapper returns a raw stack trace where every sibling returns a domain error.

Consistent examples: `src/app/api/tax/ares/route.ts` (400 for bad IČO, 404 not-found-in-ARES, 502 for upstream non-2xx/non-JSON, catch-all 502 in catch block lines 57-59); `src/app/api/vat/validate/route.ts:71-104` same shape. Divergent example: `src/app/api/tax/submit/route.ts` POST handler has zero try/catch around `await request.json()`, `db.prepare(...).get()`, or `sendMessage()` — an malformed body or DB exception here would 500 with an unhandled stack trace instead of the domain envelope used elsewhere.

### Separate a stale-deploy chunk failure from a render error _(proposed for this repo)_

A chunk that fails to load after a deploy is not a render error: the code the user is running no longer exists on the server, and a retry will never fix it. Pattern-match the bundler's chunk-load failure shapes inside the boundary and show a refresh-for-new-version message instead, and expose a reset key so navigation can clear the boundary without a full reload.

`src/components/layout/ChunkErrorBoundary.tsx:16-27` `isChunkLoadError()` regex-matches five known chunk-failure message shapes across bundlers. `componentDidUpdate` (36-40) resets error state when `resetKey` changes (used when switching module tabs, per the comment at line 8-9). `componentDidCatch` (42-52) explicitly notes a privacy intent: 'Surface enough detail ... without leaking anything user-data-shaped — only error name, message, and component path.'

### Don't collapse integration failures into null or an empty list _(proposed for this repo)_

Wrapping every call to an external client so it returns a sentinel — false, null, an empty list — spares callers a try/catch and destroys the only information they need. A caller cannot tell 'the service answered no' from 'the network failed', so no sensible retry policy can be written. If you must swallow, swallow into a typed result that still names the cause.

`src/lib/isds/client.ts:66-120` `sendMessage()` catches all exceptions to `{success:false, error: err.message}` (114-119); `getDeliveryInfo()` (125-151) swallows to `null` on any error (148-150); `findDataBox()` (156-186) swallows to `[]` (183-185). All three lose the distinction between 'ISDS said no' and 'network/DNS/TLS failed' — a caller retry policy can't tell whether retrying is sensible.

### Type error variants only where a caller matches on them _(proposed for this repo)_

Typed error enums earn their cost only where a caller actually matches on the variants; for an internal service with no public error contract, a context chain annotated at each fallible call reads better and moves faster. Pick one stance per crate or module and back it with a lint against bare unwraps, rather than mixing both and getting neither the exhaustive match nor the readable chain.

`grep -rln thiserror crates/*/src/*.rs` returns zero matches; `anyhow::Result`/`use anyhow` appears in 56 files. Example: `crates/brainiac-store/src/lib.rs:52,56,78,96` — every fallible call chained with `.context("...")`. `[workspace.lints.clippy] unwrap_used = "warn"` in `Cargo.toml:60` backs this with a lint (a bare `unwrap()` outside test code is a lint warning, and the codebase largely honors it — only 1 non-test `unwrap()` hit in the crates/ scan).

### Make throttling a typed error, never an empty result _(proposed for this repo)_

Rate limits and quota caps arrive from every provider in a different shape, and returning an empty result for them makes a gap indistinguishable from ground truth. Normalize the provider-specific throttle signatures into one predicate, raise a dedicated error type, and let callers branch on that type to preserve their cursor and report 'retry' rather than committing the gap as data.

`lib/chain.ts:55-62` defines `RpcRateLimitedError`; `lib/chain.ts:110-129` `isThrottle()` normalizes ~12 different provider-specific throttle signatures (429, 402, -32001, "archive", "quota", ...) into one check, applied in `headBlock`, `fetchSwapLogs`, `fetchBlockTimestamps`. `lib/dune.ts:22` defines `DuneError`. `lib/scan.ts:185-193` catches `DuneError` specifically to set `cp.status = "paused"` with `cp.error = "dune_error"` and a user-facing note, while any other error rethrows to the generic catch at `lib/scan.ts:135-141`. Comment at `lib/chain.ts:49-54` explicitly names this 'the org standard `throttle-is-a-typed-error`'.

### Route client-facing failures through one sanitizing chokepoint _(proposed for this repo)_

Raw driver, model and filesystem errors leak schema names, file paths, key hints and prompt fragments the moment they are echoed into a URL or a stream payload. Route every catch that reports to the client through one function that logs the real error server-side under a stable context tag and returns a single fixed generic message.

`src/lib/errors.ts:1-23`: "Raw error messages from SQLite/PGlite, Gemini, or the filesystem can leak schema names, file paths, API-key hints, and prompt fragments into URL query strings (?error=...) and NDJSON stream payloads. Every catch block that echoes a failure to the client routes the error through here instead." `sanitizeActionError` both `console.error`s the real error (for ops to grep by context tag) and returns the constant `GENERIC_ERROR_MESSAGE = "Something went wrong. Please try again."`.

### Standardize one parse-result shape across every form validator _(proposed for this repo)_

Feature-local validators drift into several slightly different result shapes, and every consumer then has to handle each one. Define one canonical parse result in a shared module, converge the divergent shapes onto it at the parser boundary, and fix the naming convention for whole-form parsers versus single-field coercers so the contract is guessable rather than looked up.

`parse-result.ts:1-18`: "Canonical FormData-validation result contract (ADR-0015)... Chosen because 3 of the 4 pre-existing feature copies already used `value`/`error: string`. The fourth (org-profile) carried a multi-error `errors: string[]`; that case is preserved by joining at the parser boundary." Naming convention documented alongside: whole-form parsers are `parseXyzForm(formData): ParseResult<T>`, single-field coercers are `validateXyz/parseXyz(...): ParseResult<T>`.

### Resolve null, access and shaping once at the data-adapter seam _(proposed for this repo)_

Null-handling, access validation and response shaping get re-implemented at every route unless the adapter seam resolves them once. Have every adapter method return one result union with a small closed set of error kinds, provide combinators that collapse the repeated try/catch tail, and log store faults where the error is constructed rather than trusting each call site to remember.

`src/lib/data/adapters/result.ts:1-100`. Helper combinators `wrapStore`, `wrapFound` (boolean 'did a live row match?' -> not_found on false), and `wrapVersion` (null -> unconfigured) collapse the repeated try/catch tail. `store_error` causes are logged exactly once at construction in `err()` (line 93-95) rather than trusting every call site to remember logging. HTTP shaping is deliberately kept in a sibling `http.ts` so this module stays framework-free and loads under the `tsx --test` runner with zero infra.

### Funnel every client fetch into one typed error with a timeout _(proposed for this repo)_

A browser fetch has no inherent timeout, so a hung route leaves the promise unsettled forever. Funnel every call through one helper that applies a per-call abort timeout and converts transport failures, timeouts and malformed success bodies into a single typed error — then expose the one discriminator callers actually branch on, so a payment or quota state never gets string-matched.

`src/lib/apiClient.ts:52-65` ApiClientError + isPaywall getter. Lines 79-84: per-call timeouts (`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=60_000`, `BALANCE_TIMEOUT_MS=10_000`) because "the browser→route fetch has no inherent timeout, so a hung/cold/stuck route ... would otherwise leave the promise unsettled forever." Lines 141-151: a malformed/empty 2xx body is caught and re-mapped to ApiClientError instead of throwing a raw parse error.

### Log auth failures loudly only when they signal misconfiguration _(proposed for this repo)_

Session verification fails constantly in normal operation — expired cookies, revoked tokens — so logging every failure trains operators to ignore the channel and hides the one failure that matters. Split expected token failures from credential and project misconfiguration, log only the latter, and put the diagnosis hint in the message so a half-configured deploy cannot masquerade as routine mass logout.

`src/lib/auth/session.ts:91-107`: catches Firebase `verifySessionCookie` errors, tests `err.code` against `/expired|revoked|invalid-session-cookie|argument-error/i`; only non-matching (i.e. true config/credential) errors get `logError(...)` with a diagnosis hint in the message itself ('check Firebase Admin credentials / projectId'). Comment labels this 'authentication #5', implying a numbered incident/lesson series tracked in-repo.

### Load feature data in a loader that degrades, never throws _(proposed for this repo)_

A feature's data read should never be able to break the page that introduces it. Put the read in a per-feature server-side loader that catches everything and returns an empty result, keep the page itself thin, and let the presentational component decide what to render when given nothing — sample content, a hidden section, or a retry affordance.

`features/votetrack/getVoteThemes.ts:1-9` doc comment: "Degrades gracefully to null... so introducing the store read can never break the page." `app/hlasovani/page.tsx` shows the full chain: `const themeData = await getVoteThemes(); return <VoteTrackPage themeData={themeData} />;`. Confirmed identical shape across `features/{civicscore,lawwatch,money,profile,votetrack}/get*Data.ts` — all end in `catch { return null; }` or `catch { return []; }`.

### A lint on catch-block shape does not enforce its own intent _(proposed for this repo)_

A rule that flags empty catch blocks is satisfied by a catch that returns a default, so a codebase can pass its own no-silent-catch gate while swallowing every error unlogged. Check the intent, not the shape: if the rule exists because the next person debugging production needs a signal, the gate has to assert that a signal is actually emitted.

Rule text at `eslint-rules/no-silent-catch.cjs:1-14` recommends `Sentry.captureException(err)`. Loader catches at `features/money/getMoneyData.ts:200-202`, `features/profile/getProfileData.ts:179-181`, `features/lawwatch/getLawData.ts:66-72` (two nested catches, one for a malformed artifact file, one outer) all just `return null`/`return []` with zero logging. Compare to `features/money/reviewActions.ts:81-85`, which DOES log: `catch (err) { console.warn("[submitReviewDecision] revalidatePath failed; write still succeeded", err); }` — showing the team knows how to log-on-catch when they choose to.

### Never let a best-effort follow-up fail a confirmed write _(proposed for this repo)_

A step that runs after a write has already committed — cache revalidation, an index refresh, a notification — must not be able to report the write as failed. Wrap it in its own catch that logs and swallows, so a transient downstream fault or a call outside a request scope cannot turn an honest success into a reported error.

`features/money/reviewActions.ts:76-85`: comment "the write already succeeded, so a revalidation failure... must not turn an honest success into a reported error", implemented as a nested try/catch with `console.warn` — the one loader catch in the repo that DOES log.

### Have repository writes return ok/error for domain failures _(proposed for this repo)_

A repository method that throws when the target row is missing forces every caller into a catch that can only guess at the cause. Return the ok/error union for expected domain failures — not found, already in the target state — and keep exceptions for infrastructure faults, so one result shape carries from the data layer through the action to the UI.

`lib/db/store.ts:148-169` JSDoc: "Errors (rather than throwing) when the tie doesn't exist, so callers can render an honest message instead of a stack trace." Consumed in `reviewActions.ts:71-75`: `if (!result.ok) return result.error === "tie not found" ? {status:"not-found"} : {status:"error", message: result.error};`

### Carry the client-fault distinction in the error enum itself _(proposed for this repo)_

Most error variants are the server's fault and belong on the same status; only a few are the caller's. Give the core error type one explicit client-fault variant, map that at the HTTP boundary and default everything else to a server error, letting handlers raise the situational statuses themselves. Pair it with a stable machine code in the envelope so consumers branch on the code, never on the human message.

`crates/core/src/error.rs:23-27` — `BadRequest` doc comment: "maps to HTTP 400 at the request boundary — unlike Parse, which also covers server-internal decode failures (HTTP 500)". `crates/server/src/routes/error.rs:43-54` — the `From` impl matches `BadRequest` → `StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST`, `other => StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`. The envelope (`ApiError::into_response`, lines 36-41) always returns `{error, code}` where `code` is a stable machine string derived from status (`error_code`, lines 25-34) — so API consumers can branch on `code` without string-matching the human message.

### Map HTTP status to user copy in one place, not per component _(proposed for this repo)_

Status-to-copy mapping written inline at each call site produces inconsistent wording and gaps for the statuses nobody remembered. Type the client error with its status and details, and centralize the mapping to title, message and severity in one module — exported both as a hook and as a plain function so non-component code shares exactly the same copy.

`src/app/types/ApiError.ts:5-24` — `ApiError extends Error` with `Object.setPrototypeOf` for correct `instanceof` across the transpile boundary. `src/app/hooks/useApiErrorHandler.ts:76-183` — `mapApiErrorToUserMessage` switches on `error.status` to produce copy + severity; both a hook (memoized) and a plain function (`getErrorMessage`) are exported so non-component code can reuse the same mapping.

### A degraded path must be classified and logged, never silently swallowed _(proposed for this repo)_

Every catch that returns a safe default must first classify the failure — transient provider/infra outage vs expected content or config failure — and emit a server-side signal for the transient class; returning null/false/[] with no telemetry is not graceful degradation, it is an unobservable outage.

**Why this is one shared problem**

This is one shared problem — how a request survives a dependency failure without lying to the user or to the operator — and the portfolio has both poles of the answer. Four projects built explicit failure taxonomies; two collapse everything to a bare sentinel, and politicas' own harvest flags this as violating the no-silent-catch doctrine it deliberately ported.

**Current approaches**

- **Apprenticeship Placement** — LlmUnavailableError separates genuinely transient provider failure (surfaces as an actionable 429/500) from content failure (parse failure degrades silently to a deterministic heuristic).
- **ai-bookkeeper** — Providers uniformly return null to callers, but a separate recordAiFailure telemetry seam reclassifies why — 'not-configured' stays silent, everything else (timeout, provider-error, parse-error, ungrounded-number) is recorded.
- **Medical Bill Negotiator** — Session verification splits expected token failures (expired/revoked — log silently) from real misconfiguration (bad service account, wrong project) which gets a loud logError.
- **politicas** — Every per-feature server loader wraps its whole body in `catc

### Boundary parsers must return a reason, through one canonical result contract _(proposed for this repo)_

Every request/form validator at a trust boundary should return one workspace-canonical discriminated union carrying the failure reason — not `T | null`, which throws away the only information the caller needs to tell the user what was wrong.

**Why this is one shared problem**

All three apps validate untrusted request shapes at the same seam, and Grant Writing Nonprofits already documents (ADR-0015) that four ad hoc shapes converging on one ParseResult was a win. Whether the implementation is zod or hand-written is a defensible dependency choice and not the divergence; the return contract is, and `T | null` is strictly lossier.

**Current approaches**

- **Grant Writing Nonprofits** — One canonical ParseResult<T> = {ok:true;value} | {ok:false;error} that every feature's validation.ts returns, replacing four previously divergent ad hoc shapes.
- **Apprenticeship Placement** — GuardOptions.parse is a repo-wide idiom of hand-written (raw: unknown) => T | null functions across ~15 metered routes, documented as a deliberate 'no zod' choice — the null carries no reason.
- **auto-invoicer** — A zod invoiceSchema is the single source of truth; validateInvoice() folds safeParse issues into a flat {dotted.path: message} map consumed per-field by form components.

### Discriminated result unions at domain boundaries, exceptions only for programmer error _(proposed for this repo)_

Functions whose failure a caller might reasonably handle return an {ok:true,...} | {ok:false,...} union rather than throwing across module or network lines; thrown exceptions are reserved for genuinely exceptional conditions.

**Independently converged on by 6 projects**

- ai-paralegal
- Grant Writing Nonprofits
- Immigration Paperwork
- politicas
- auto-invoicer
- Pumper

A pattern this many projects reached independently is a candidate workspace-wide standard.

### A fallback layer hides absence: check translated VALUES, not just key parity _(proposed for this repo)_

When a runtime fallback silently substitutes a default (English under every locale, a default config under every tenant), a parity check on KEYS proves nothing. Add a second gate that asserts the VALUE actually differs from the fallback, scoped to live (source-referenced) entries, with an explicit allowlist for legitimately-identical values.

`src/i18n/useTranslation.ts` exposes a `t` Proxy that deep-merges English under every locale, so a missing translation renders English with no warning. `scripts/i18n/check-coverage.mjs` reported "0 missing" and was green — while ~57k raw-English strings (~24% of the app) sat behind it until 2026-07-12.

The fix is a companion gate, wired into `lefthook.yml` pre-commit alongside the key gate:

```yaml
- name: i18n-no-gaps
  glob: "src/i18n/locales/*.json"
  run: node scripts/i18n/check-coverage.mjs --strict   # KEY parity

- name: i18n-no-untranslated
  glob: "src/i18n/locales/*.json"
  run: node scripts/i18n/check-untranslated.mjs --strict # VALUE parity
```

`check-untranslated.mjs` header states the rule directly: *"A key can exist in every locale and still render English — the runtime `t` Proxy deep-merges English underneath, so nothing warns. This script is the missing half."* Two design details make it usable rather than noisy: dead keys (no source call site, found via `find-unused-i18n-keys.mjs`) are excluded because they are never rendered, and `docs/i18n/untranslated-allowlist.json` carries `<lang>:<key>` exemptions for values that are correctly identical.

Independent classifiers — retryability, user-facing copy, UI guidance — drift apart and force every call site to run all three over the same string. Collapse them behind one call that returns a single classified object, and give the user-facing result an explicit intent category so each surface picks its treatment from data rather than from string matching.

`src/lib/errors/errorPipeline.ts`:

> Combines the three error classification systems into a single pass:
> 1. `errorTaxonomy` → ErrorCategory + severity + retryability + failover
> 2. `errorRegistry` → user-facing message + suggestion (toasts)
> 3. `errorExplanation` → UI-specific guidance + severity + navigation action

The categorization in `src/lib/errors/errorRegistry.ts` is what makes the output actionable — it encodes *who can fix this*, which is the only distinction the UI actually needs:

- `recoverable` — transient/self-healing, presented as "we caught that for you" rather than a hard error state.
- `user_action` — validation, bad passphrase, expired session.
- `system` — CLI not installed, network offline, corrupted bundle.

### Attach realtime subscriptions in priority waves, retry failures on a budget, then tell the user _(proposed for this repo)_

Cold-start listener registration will intermittently fail. Attach critical channels first, yield a frame, bulk-register the rest, retry the failures on a bounded backoff schedule detached from startup — and if the budget is exhausted, surface a non-blocking 'updates may be delayed' toast instead of leaving the UI silently half-wired.

`src/lib/eventBridge.ts` centralises every Tauri `listen()` into a declarative `registry` where each entry has `event`, `setup()` returning unlisten handles, and `priority: "critical" | "normal"`.

`initAllListeners()` runs wave 1 (auth/persona/execution) in parallel, awaits a single `requestAnimationFrame` "so the renderer can paint and accept input before we submit the bulk IPC traffic", then wave 2 in batches of 16. Every wave is bracketed with `performance.mark`/`measure` so the cost is visible in DevTools.

Failures are collected, not logged-and-forgotten, and retried on `LISTENER_RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [500, 1500, 4500]`:

> the original `Promise.allSettled` loop logged and forgot them, leaving the UI partially wired with no recovery path other than an app restart

Retries run detached — "partial wiring is preferable to making startup wait on flaky IPC retries". After the budget:

```ts
useToastStore.getState().addToast(
  "Some real-time updates may be delayed. Restart the app if data appears stale.", "error", 8000);
```

### Treat a dirty section with no save callback as a save failure _(proposed for this repo)_

In a registry that fans a save across independently-registered sections, the missing-callback branch is the one that lies: marking the section clean produces an all-saved confirmation for data that was never written. Treat it as a save failure, keep the section dirty, log it as the wiring bug it is, and carry both the failed and the succeeded sets so partial success is reported honestly.

`src/features/agents/sub_editor/libs/EditorDocument.tsx`, inside `saveAll()`:

```ts
  // "all saved" outcome — the user's toast was a lie.
  logger.error('Dirty tab has no registered save callback', { tab });

}
```

A creation flow that ends in a fixed success notification will eventually announce readiness for something that cannot run. Read the result payload before choosing the wording and name what is outstanding — unmet credentials, entities that failed to create — because a generic 'ready to use' is exactly the silent failure that burns a non-technical user.

A bulk endpoint should never be all-or-nothing and never a bare count. Return the succeeded ids plus per-id failure reasons as machine tokens.   // reason tokens: retry_exhausted | not_found | wrong_status → localized labels
```ts
  …
```

### Warn when you rewrite a value to satisfy a platform limit _(proposed for this repo)_

Clamping, coercing or defaulting a user-supplied value without saying so produces a UI that confirms something the system will not do. Give the parse or normalize result a warnings channel carrying a coded, human-readable advisory whenever a value was rewritten, and render it beside the accepted result rather than in a log.

`src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/nlTriggerParser.ts` names the anti-pattern:

```ts
/**
 * Non-fatal advisory emitted when the parser rewrote a user-supplied value to
 * satisfy a platform constraint. Previously the parser silently clamped
 * sub-minute interval values to 60s, so the user saw "every 5 seconds"
 * accepted but the trigger actually ran every 60 seconds — classic Success
 * Theater. The UI renders these warnings inline next to the parsed result.
 */
export interface NlParseWarning { code: 'interval_clamped'; message: string; }
export interface NlParseResult {
  triggerType: string; label: string; confidence: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low';
  formOverrides: Partial<TriggerFormState>; warnings: NlParseWarning[];
}
```

The warning carries both a machine `code` and a message that states the constraint and what was substituted:

```ts
ctx.warnings.push({ code: 'interval_clamped',
  message: `Intervals below ${MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS}s are not supported. Clamped "every ${n} ${unit}…" to ${MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS}s — the minimum schedule interval.` });
```
