## frontend

### Own durable state on the server; keep client state ephemeral _(proposed for this repo)_

When the server can be the single owner of durable state, client components need no global store at all — tenant-scoped server-side stores hold everything durable and components keep only ephemeral UI state. The alternative mirrors server data into a client store and then spends its life reconciling two sources of truth.

package.json dependencies list (no state-management library present). `src/features/matters/store.ts:154-193` and `src/features/demand-letter/counter-offer-store.ts:8-20` both register through `defineFeatureStore()` (src/lib/db/feature-store.ts) — a generic tenant-scoped async CRUD adapter backed by Firestore in prod / in-memory Maps in dev (`dbDriver()` switch, feature-store.ts:14-16). This is a deliberate RSC-first architecture: state ownership sits on the server, client state is local/derived only.

### Refetch after each mutation instead of keeping a client cache _(proposed for this repo)_

With the database as the sole source of truth, each panel can hold local state and re-fetch its own endpoint after every mutation — no client cache means no stale-cache bugs. The cost is that every panel re-implements the loading/error/refetch triangle by hand, so this only holds while the panel count stays small.

grep for `zustand|createStore` across `src/` returns zero hits; 22 files use local `useState`/`useReducer`. Each dashboard component (e.g. `src/components/employers/JobComposer.tsx`, `src/components/employers/PlacementBoard.tsx`, `src/components/team/TeamPanel.tsx`) calls `fetch('/api/...')` directly inline and re-fetches the list after a POST/DELETE to resync — no client cache layer (no SWR/React Query either). This keeps the client thin and avoids stale-cache bugs but means every panel re-implements its own loading/error/refetch triangle by hand.

### Fold schema issues into a path-keyed error map before the UI _(proposed for this repo)_

Let one schema be the canonical shape of the entity, then flatten its validation issues into a flat map keyed by dotted field path so each control reads only its own message. Exposing the validator's raw issue array to components makes every field re-implement the search for its own error.

`src/lib/invoice/validation.ts:78-94` — `validateInvoice` reduces zod issues to `ValidationErrors` keyed by `issue.path.join(".")`, keeping only the first message per path (line 88-90). Schemas compose via nested zod objects (`partySchema`, `lineItemSchema`, `paymentDetailsSchema` at lines 4-28) reused for both `supplier` and `customer`. Custom date validation via `.refine()` chains (lines 32-41) rather than a date-specific zod type, showing a preference for explicit refine-based messages over relying on zod's built-in date coercion.

### Derive every primitive's classes from one shared token hook _(proposed for this repo)_

With a small fixed set of themes and no component library, put every primitive's class strings behind a single token hook that branches on the theme once; each primitive then consumes named tokens instead of owning styling logic. Know the ceiling this buys: a third theme means touching every token, which is the signal to move to a real token file.

`src/components/ui/FormKit.tsx:25-76` `useFormTokens()` returns ~30 named Tailwind-class fields (sectionBg, inputBorder, focusRing, primaryBg, ...) each with an inline mono/warm ternary. Every primitive (`Section` 80-93, `TextInput` 115-134, `SecurePasswordInput` 142-218, `PrimaryButton` 355-365) consumes `f.<field>` rather than owning its own styling logic. This centralizes the two-theme system but means adding a third theme requires touching every field in `useFormTokens` rather than an isolated token file — a scaling cost worth knowing about if the theme count grows.

### Share one small client-only value with a module-level pub/sub _(proposed for this repo)_

A single small value shared by a handful of components does not justify a state library: module-level functions over local storage plus a listener set and a subscribing hook give cross-component and cross-tab sync in a few dozen lines. The failure this replaces is not a missing library but the same logic inlined per file.

`app/components/follow-store.ts:11-52`: `listeners: Set<() => void>` fan-out, `toggleFollow()` writes localStorage then calls every listener and dispatches a `storage` event so other tabs/components resync; `useFollowed()` subscribes/unsubscribes in a `useEffect`. Comment at line 7-8: 'Replaces the copies that were inlined per-file' — i.e. this was itself a dedup refactor, not the original shape.

### Re-run one load callback on mount and after every mutation _(proposed for this repo)_

Without a data-fetching library, keep fetching predictable by giving each surface exactly one load callback that aggregates its calls and is re-run after any mutation. Accept explicitly that there is then no caching, dedupe or staleness layer anywhere — that absence is the design, and discovering it later is what hurts.

`app/components/pipeline.tsx:14-27` `load()` does `Promise.all([fetch("/api/scan"), fetch("/api/library/tokens"), fetch("/api/players")])` guarded with `.catch(() => null)` per-call, then conditionally sets state only if the shape looks ok (`t?.ok`). `runJob()` (lines 29-37) POSTs a step then calls `load()` again to refresh. Consistent pattern; no caching/dedup/staleness layer exists anywhere in the repo.

### Hydrate from local storage first, then reconcile with the server _(proposed for this repo)_

Cross-cutting state that must work offline and signed-out belongs in one context that hydrates locally on mount and then reconciles against the server copy for authenticated users, with a documented winner and a one-time backfill. Treat a failed server call as non-fatal and keep the local copy; prop-drilling the same state instead scatters the reconciliation policy across every consumer.

`src/features/bill-analysis/CaseMetaContext.tsx:17-38` doc comment: 'Previously this state lived inside AnalyzeBillPanel and was prop-drilled... Lifting it into a context lets each consumer read and mutate it directly.' Persistence is explicitly two-tier: localStorage always-on, server mirror via `/api/case-meta` (ADR-012) only when a user is signed in AND a Store is configured; a failed server call is treated as non-fatal (keep the local copy). `chooseHydratedMeta` in `caseMetaSync.ts` implements the reconciliation policy separately from the context component.

### Keep the shared catalog domain-free, and let a lint rule enforce it _(proposed for this repo)_

A primitives catalog stays reusable only if its components cannot reach into features or domain data — everything they need must arrive through props. Scope an import restriction to the catalog directory so the boundary is machine-checked; a convention stated only in a README erodes within a few sprints.

`eslint.config.mjs:48-66`: `files: ["features/shared/components/**/*.{ts,tsx}"]` with `no-restricted-imports` patterns `["@/features/*", "!@/features/shared"]` and a matching lib/civic ban, both with explicit error messages pointing back at "pass data via props, or move the component to its owning feature." `SourceNote.tsx` itself takes only `children`/`tone`/`dot`/`className` props, no store or feature imports.

### Give every entity one hook module owning its client and its cache _(proposed for this repo)_

Route all entity CRUD through per-entity modules that export both the API client and the query hooks built on it, so cache keys, invalidation and optimistic updates live beside the calls they govern. Old import paths can survive as thin re-export shims rather than forcing a repo-wide rename.

`src/app/api/characters.ts` is a 6-line re-export: `export { characterApi } from '../hooks/integration/useCharacters';`. 24 integration hook files exist (`useActs`, `useBeats`, `useCharacters`, `useFactions`, `useRelationships`, `useScenes`, `useVideos`, `useVoices`, etc.), all colocated under `src/app/hooks/integration/`. `useOptimisticMutation` (see `src/app/hooks/useOptimisticMutation.example.tsx`) layers optimistic updates + toast + undo on top of these API clients, keyed by `affectedQueryKeys` for cache invalidation.

### Split global state into many small stores, not one combined object _(proposed for this repo)_

Independently-imported stores per concern keep subscriptions narrow and tree-shaking effective, while a combined root store is a convenience that quietly re-renders unrelated surfaces. Where a combined accessor exists, document it as the exception, and keep superseded flat stores as re-export shims so the migration path stays visible instead of looking like drift.

`src/app/store/index.ts:36-54` — `useRootStore` combines `project` + `character` slices but is explicitly commented 'use sparingly' / 'components should prefer importing individual slices directly'. `src/app/store/characterStore.ts` and `projectStore.ts` are `@deprecated` thin re-export shims pointing at `slices/characterSlice.ts` / `slices/projectSlice.ts` — a clean, intentional migration path (not drift) from old flat store files to the newer `slices/` convention.

### Put the loading delay on the placeholder, never on the content _(proposed for this repo)_

Data already on screen is never hidden, dimmed, or replaced by a refetch; content renders the instant it exists. The anti-flash delay lives entirely on the skeleton — a CSS `animation-delay` of ≥120ms with `fill-mode: both`, so a fast fetch never paints a ghost — and life comes from a one-shot, id-guarded per-row cascade rather than a whole-block cross-fade.

`docs/design/overview-loading.md` is the repo's single source of truth, with `src/features/overview/sub_activity/components/GlobalExecutionList.tsx` as the reference implementation. v1 of the doc prescribed a whole-region cross-fade gate (`LoadingReveal` + `useStableLoading`); live use proved it wrong (skeleton on every visit, content held after data arrived, one big-bang reveal) and v2 deprecated it. That reversal is the evidence — the pattern is battle-tested, not theoretical.

The five laws:
1. **Data on screen is sacred** — a fetch never hides/dims/replaces rendered rows; a loading flag decides only what an *empty* region shows.
2. **Content is never held** — no minimum placeholder duration, no `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` swap (exit-then-enter *is* a forced delay).
3. **The delay lives on the placeholder** — ghosts enter via `animate-fade-in` behind a staggered `animation-delay` starting ≥120ms. "That CSS delay *is* the anti-flash: zero timers, zero JS, nothing ever waits on it."
4. **Life comes from item-level cascade** — 35ms stagger, first viewport only, one-shot and id-guarded so polling/scrolling never replay it.
5. **Static chrome always renders** — header

### Tombstone deleted ids so an in-flight fetch can't resurrect them _(proposed for this repo)_

Optimistic delete plus a wholesale list refresh is a race: a fetch that started before the delete resolves with a pre-delete snapshot and undoes the removal. Keep short-lived tombstones, filter them out of every incoming snapshot, and retire each one when a fresh snapshot confirms the row is gone so the set stays bounded.

`src/stores/slices/vault/credentialSlice.ts` carries `recentlyDeletedCredentialIds: Set<string>` alongside `pendingDeleteCredentialIds`. `deleteCredential` adds the id on success; `fetchCredentials` filters the incoming snapshot:

```ts
const credentials = fetched.filter((c) => !tombstones.has(c.id));
// Retire tombstones the backend has caught up on — an id no longer
// present in a fresh snapshot can never be resurrected again, so it
// need not be tracked. Allocate a new set only if something changes.
```

The self-retiring step is what keeps the set bounded (it does not grow one entry per delete forever), and the slice only allocates a new `Set` when something actually changed, so React/Zustand subscribers don't churn.

The file's header comment names the exact seam the TTL cache could *not* paper over: "the one race the TTL can't paper over is delete vs. an already-in-flight fetch". That is the general lesson — caching and optimistic mutation interact, and the interaction needs its own mechanism.

### Centralise the latest-wins token so the compare is right once _(proposed for this repo)_

Stale-response guards get reimplemented per slice and get the comparison backwards, so whichever request resolves last wins even when its data is older. Extract one tiny primitive that mints a token and answers whether the caller is still the newest, and consult it in both the success and the failure branch so a stale failure cannot clear a fresh load flag.

`src/stores/util/latestWins.ts` is the whole primitive: `next()` mints a token, `isCurrent(token)` answers "am I still the newest". Its docstring names the failure it prevents:

> Without this, two concurrent fetches (StrictMode double-mount, rapid filter/route changes, auto-refresh racing a manual refresh) can race and whichever resolves LAST wins — even when its data is older.

And the reason it exists as a module rather than a copy-paste: "Centralizing the counter/compare pair here means the comparison direction (and the 'am I still current' question) only needs to be gotten right once." The docstring includes the canonical usage — check `isCurrent` in **both** the success and the catch branch, so a stale failure doesn't clear a fresh load flag.

This is a good template for the general move: when N slices grow the same 6 lines independently, the extraction's value is correctness-per-instance, not LOC saved.

### Retry a failed chunk import, but keep one stable lazy instance _(proposed for this repo)_

Wrap dynamic imports with one retry, but keep a single `React.lazy` instance. Creating a fresh lazy inside the failing promise's `.catch` races React's error propagation and re-suspends instead of throwing, so an unreachable chunk shows an infinite skeleton with no recovery.

`src/lib/lazyRetry.ts` carries the whole post-mortem:

> **Why not swap to a fresh `React.lazy` on rejection?** An earlier version did exactly that ... But the swap raced React's error propagation: React remounts the suspended child when its promise settles, so it rendered the fresh *pending* lazy and **re-suspended** instead of throwing the rejection to the boundary. Against a permanently-unreachable chunk this looped forever — the user saw an **infinite loading skeleton** and never the recoverable error UI.

The shipped shape: `importWithRetry` retries once after 1.5s (covers transient blips and stale post-deploy hashes); a permanent rejection propagates to the nearest ErrorBoundary, whose chunk-error UI offers "Reload app" — because "resetting the boundary alone can't fix a chunk that no longer exists".

`isChunkLoadError` is exported separately and matches all three engine messages (Chromium/WebView2, WebKit, Firefox), which is what lets the boundary distinguish a chunk failure from a render bug and offer the right action.

### Make the unmount guard automatic in the hook, never opt-in _(proposed for this repo)_

If safety requires the call site to invoke a returned `cleanup()`, most call sites won't — the protection silently never runs. Make the guard automatic inside the hook, and make it re-arm on mount so StrictMode's double-invoke doesn't leave it disarmed.

`src/hooks/utility/interaction/useAsyncAction.ts` — the canonical loading/error wrapper the repo pushes over hand-rolled `useState` pairs ("the codebase has ~70% of component fetches doing so"):

```ts
// Auto unmount-safety: flip mountedRef on real unmount so execute() never
// set-states after unmount, with zero caller wiring. (Previously this was
// opt-in via the returned `cleanup`, which most call sites never invoked —
// so the guard silently did nothing.) The effect re-sets true on mount to
// stay correct under StrictMode's mount→unmount→mount double-invoke.
useEffect(() => { mountedRef.current = true; return () => { mountedRef.current = false; }; }, []);
```

The `mountedRef` check gates `onSuccess`, `onError`, the error `setState` **and** the `finally` `setLoading(false)`. `cleanup` is retained only for back-compat.

The same discipline shows up in `src/hooks/useTauriEvent.ts`, where the async `listen()` cleanup race is handled inside the hook rather than being re-derived at each call site: "The cancelled flag is needed because `listen()` is async; if the component unmounts (or the effect re-runs) before the subscription resolves, we have to tear down whatever did

### Group draft fields per save operation and assert coverage in types _(proposed for this repo)_

Model the editable entity as one flat draft type, then declare a `readonly` key array per save group (per tab / per backend operation). Derive dirty detection, baseline updates and save payloads from those arrays, and add a type-level assertion that every draft key belongs to exactly one group — so adding a field without wiring its save is a typecheck error, not a silent no-op.

`src/features/agents/sub_editor/libs/PersonaDraft.ts` defines `PersonaDraft` plus `SETTINGS_KEYS` and `MODEL_KEYS` (`as const satisfies readonly (keyof PersonaDraft)[]`), then:

```ts
type _CoveredKeys = (typeof SETTINGS_KEYS)[number] | (typeof MODEL_KEYS)[number];
type _AssertAllCovered = keyof PersonaDraft extends _CoveredKeys ? true : never;
type _AssertNoExtra = _CoveredKeys extends keyof PersonaDraft ? true : never;
const _exhaustiveCheck: _AssertAllCovered & _AssertNoExtra = true;
```

The same arrays then drive everything downstream: `draftChanged(draft, baseline, keys)` for dirty detection, `pickKeys(d, SETTINGS_KEYS)` for the `setBaseline` payload, and the debounce `deps` in `src/features/agents/sub_editor/libs/useEditorSave.ts` (`deps: MODEL_KEYS.map((k) => draft[k])`). One list, four consumers — the field lists can't drift.

### Persist an undo before moving the baseline, or it silently vanishes _(proposed for this repo)_

In an autosaving editor, implementing undo by moving the baseline back makes the field look clean, so the autosave never reconciles storage with the undone value: the DB keeps the post-save value while the header reads 'All saved', and the undo evaporates on reload. Persist the restored state first, and only then move the baseline; on failure leave the section dirty and surface the error.

From `makeUndoEntry` in `src/features/agents/sub_editor/libs/useEditorSave.ts`:

> "Undo/redo must be a real persistence round-trip, not just an in-memory draft+baseline swap. Moving baseline alone made settingsDirty false, so the debounced autosave never reconciled disk with the undone state — the DB silently kept the post-save value while the header read 'All saved', and the undo was discarded on the next reload. Persist first, then move baseline; on failure leave the tab dirty and surface the error."

Both `restore` and `reapply` route through the same `buildSettingsOp` / `buildModelOp` builders the normal save uses, so an undo persists in exactly the shape a manual edit would. The stack itself (`src/features/agents/sub_editor/libs/EditorDocument.tsx`) pushes the entry back on if `restore()` throws, and is capped at `MAX_UNDO_DEPTH = 50`.

### Drive the router from a typed registry with a completeness guard _(proposed for this repo)_

### Pin a virtualized group header through the range extractor _(proposed for this repo)_

To pin a group header in a virtualizer, override the range extractor to always include the nearest header at-or-above the viewport top, and store which one is active in a ref rather than state — the virtualizer already re-renders on scroll, and a setState inside the extractor is a render loop. Share the extractor, the header component and the flattening helper so every grouped surface pins identically.

`src/features/shared/components/display/GroupedVirtualList.tsx`:

```ts
// The header that should currently be pinned. A ref (not state) so updating it
// inside rangeExtractor never triggers a render loop — the virtualizer already
// re-renders on scroll, and the render reads `.current`.
const activeStickyRef = useRef<number>(headerIndexes[0] ?? -1);

const rangeExtractor = useCallback((range: Range) => {
  let sticky = headerIndexes[0] ?? -1;
  for (const h of headerIndexes) { if (h <= range.startIndex) sticky = h; else break; }
  activeStickyRef.current = sticky;
  const next = new Set(defaultRangeExtractor(range));
  if (sticky >= 0) next.add(sticky);
  return Array.from(next).sort((a, b) => a - b);
}, [headerIndexes]);
```

`GroupHeaderRow` swaps between `position: sticky` (pinned) and `position: absolute` + translateY (scrolling at its offset) off one `pinned` boolean, and both `useGroupedVirtualizer` and `GroupHeaderRow` are exported specifically so the column-based `UnifiedTable` renders identical mechanics rather than a second implementation.

### Queue and re-key live-region announcements so none are lost _(proposed for this repo)_

Live-region announcements pushed in the same tick collapse: React coalesces the setState calls and only the last message reaches the DOM. And an identical consecutive message is not re-announced at all. Queue announcements, flush one per interval, and bump a key on the live-region node so each message gets its own commit and its own utterance.

`src/features/shared/components/feedback/AriaLiveProvider.tsx` — both failure modes are handled and documented:

```ts

// duplicate consecutive messages.
const keyRef = useRef(0);

// A burst of announce() calls in one tick would otherwise collapse: React
// coalesces the setState calls so only the LAST message reaches the live
// region — intermediate messages are dropped and never spoken. Queue messages
// and flush one per interval so each gets its own render commit + key remount.
timerRef.current = setTimeout(drain, 150);
```

```ts

// provider may have replaced it; blindly nulling would silence the live one.

Catch name collisions at type-time rather than save-time with a debounced check that passes an AbortSignal to the caller's checker, supersedes the pending timer and in-flight request on every keystroke, and — critically — falls back to idle on error so a broken check never blocks the user. ```ts

  // A failed availability check must never block the user — fall back
  // to idle so the existing save-time validation stays the backstop.
  setStatus('idle');
}
```

Supporting details worth copying: the `check` callback is held in a ref *"so callers can pass an inline closure without re-creating `onChange` (and tearing down in-flight debounces) every render"*; the status vocabulary is deliberately distinct from blocking validation (`idle | checking | available | taken`); and a `suggestAlternativeName(base, taken)` helper produces the "try X" fallback.

### Animate collapse with grid rows, and keep the unmount you replaced _(proposed for this repo)_

Animating height forces a layout pass every frame; transitioning a single grid row from zero to one fraction gives the same smooth result without measuring the DOM. The migration hazard is the real lesson — the always-mounted form keeps effects, subscriptions and polling alive inside every closed section, so carry an explicit unmount option when replacing a presence-based collapse.

`src/features/shared/components/display/Collapse.tsx`:

> "Uses the CSS grid row trick: `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` with a transition gives a smooth height animation without measuring the DOM and without animating `height`, which forces a layout pass on every frame."

The migration hazard is called out on the prop, not left to reviewers:

> "`unmountWhenClosed` — Off by default so the original callers keep their always-mounted behaviour. Turn it ON when migrating an `<AnimatePresence>{open && …}</AnimatePresence>` collapse: that pattern unmounts its subtree, and silently dropping the unmount would leave effects, subscriptions and polling alive inside every closed section."

Two further details generalize: children stay mounted *through* the close transition and are removed on a timer afterwards (*"unmounting immediately would empty the box before it finished shrinking"*), and `revealOverflowWhenOpen` flips to `overflow: visible` only once the open transition has settled, so a dropdown inside isn't clipped but content can't spill mid-animation.

It emits **one rule per distinct colour, not per path** (*"a 50-path glyph usually carries only a dozen quantized hues"*), and the dark→light recolor is a documented perceptual rule rather than a hand-picked palette: navy ink lifts toward slate *"so it doesn't read as a hole"*, neon accents deepen ~14% *"because saturated hues vibrate against a light surface"*. ### Show an honest asymptotic bar for unknown-duration work _(proposed for this repo)_

A progress bar for work with only an *estimate* should run linearly to ~85% over the estimate, then crawl asymptotically toward ~98%, switch to an amber "taking longer" state past the estimate, and jump to 100% only when the work actually reports done. Never let it sit at 100% while work continues, and never let it stall at a number that looks stuck.

`src/features/shared/components/progress/EstimatedProgressBar.tsx`:

```ts
if (elapsedSec < estimatedSeconds) {
  p = (elapsedSec / estimatedSeconds) * 85;      // Linear phase: 0 -> 85%
} else {
  const over = elapsedSec - estimatedSeconds;    // Asymptotic crawl: 85% -> ~98%
  p = 85 + 13 * (1 - 1 / (1 + over * 0.05));
}
```

The UI states are all derived, not hand-managed: `isOvertime` tints the bar amber and swaps the "~Ns remaining" text for a "taking longer" line; the completion path cancels the rAF and jumps to 100%. The component renders `null` if it never started.

One React detail worth stealing: the tick callback is mirrored into a ref so the driver effect doesn't depend on it — *"tick's identity changes whenever estimatedSeconds changes, which would otherwise cancel and fail to reschedule the rAF loop mid-run."*

### Replace N modal booleans with one typed modal stack _(proposed for this repo)_

A screen with several dialogs accumulates a `useState` pair and a handler per dialog, and loses z-ordering. Model the open dialogs as a stack of discriminated-union entries with `open` / `close(type?)` / `replace` / `closeAll` plus typed `find` and `isOpen` — adding a dialog then costs one union member and zero state variables.

`src/features/templates/sub_generated/gallery/modals/useModalStack.ts`:

```ts
export function useModalStack<E extends { type: string }>() {
  const [stack, setStack] = useState<E[]>([]);
  …
  return { stack, open, close, replace, closeAll,
    find: <T extends E['type']>(type: T) => stack.find((e) => e.type === type) as Extract<E, { type: T }> | undefined,
    isOpen: (type: E['type']) => stack.some((e) => e.type === type),
    top: stack[stack.length - 1] as E | undefined };
}
```

The payoff is stated in the docblock: "The stack handles Z-ordering (most recent on top) and typed lookups. New modals only need a type discriminant added to the entry union -- zero new state variables or handlers in the parent component." `close(type)` removes the *most recent* entry of that type (searching from the top) rather than the first, and `replace` exists specifically for modal-to-modal transitions that shouldn't grow the stack.

### Carry a monotonic key so a repeated identical arrival still fires _(proposed for this repo)_

React bails on `setState` with an unchanged value, so a deep link or request that arrives twice with the same payload silently no-ops and the user sees a stale view. Pair every 'arrival' with a monotonically increasing key so the consumer re-triggers, and bump a request token on reset so in-flight responses from a prior arrival are discarded instead of flashing into the new one.

`src/features/settings/sub_network/components/ShareLinkHandler.tsx` documents the exact failure:

```ts
// Monotonic key bumped on every deep-link arrival. Without this, a second
// identical share URL arriving while the dialog is already open silently no-ops:
// setPendingUrl(sameUrl) and setOpen(true) both bail because the values are
// unchanged, so the dialog's autoStartedRef effect never re-fires and the user
// (who clicked their share link expecting a retry) sees the stale preview.
setShareLinkKey((k) => k + 1);
```

`BundleImportDialog.tsx` consumes `shareLinkKey` alongside the URL (`urlChanged || keyChanged`) and independently owns the discard token:

```ts
const requestTokenRef = useRef(0);
const reset = () => { requestTokenRef.current++; ... };
const token = ++requestTokenRef.current;
const p = await previewBundleImport(path);
if (token !== requestTokenRef.current) return;   // a prior open's response — drop it
```

`useTourNarration.ts` uses the same generation counter (`genRef`) so a TTS synth that resolves after the step changed is never played. Three unrelated features, one primitive.

### Float zero-setup options to the top of the first-run picker _(proposed for this repo)_

On the first-run picker, stable-partition the candidate list so options requiring no credentials/setup float to the top, keep the backend's own ordering as the tie-break within each group, and pull a larger pool than you display so the zero-setup ones can be lifted into the visible slots.

`src/features/onboarding/components/useOnboardingState.ts`:

 * Order within each group is preserved, so the backend's trending / recency
 * ordering still breaks ties.
 */

  const zeroCred = [], rest = [];
  for (const r of reviews) (parseJsonOrDefault(r.connectors_used, []).length === 0 ? zeroCred : rest).push(r);
  return [...zeroCred, ...rest];
}
...
setTemplates(prioritizeZeroCredential(reviews).slice(0, 3));
```

The complementary ranking lives in `templateRecommendation.ts`: templates are scored against the desktop apps the user just approved (`matched.length / approvedApps.size`), matched ones float up, unmatched keep their relative order. Same stable-partition discipline; the personalisation signal comes from a step the user already completed rather than a questionnaire.

### Measure adoption with a data probe, not with a 'Try it' click _(proposed for this repo)_

A feature-discovery board that marks items done because the user clicked 'Try it' measures curiosity, not adoption. Give each entry an optional `detect()` probe against real user data, promote hits to a persisted, never-unset 'done', and skip probing anything already done so the steady state costs zero IPC.

`src/features/home/sub_learning/powerMoves/registry.ts` defines the contract on the registry entry:

```ts

 * Optional honest-completion probe: returns true when the user's real data shows

 * Moves without one fall back to "tried" (clicked Try it).
 * Keep probes to a single cheap IPC call — they run on Learning-hub mount.
 */
detect?: () => Promise<boolean>;
```

`powerMovesStore.ts` holds two separate maps (`tried` vs `done`) in a persisted zustand store and states the semantics: *"Achievement semantics: once earned, a move stays done (persisted), so probes only run for moves not yet detected — steady state is zero IPC."* Each probe failure is `silentCatch`'d individually so one broken probe can't abort the sweep. The launch action (`launchPowerMove.ts`) reuses the tour engine's own section→sub-tab sequencing delay and a lightweight non-dimming spotlight (`flashSpotlight.ts`: polls for the anchor up to 4s, scrolls it into view, pulses a `pointer-events-none` ring, self-removes) rather than inventing a second navigation path.

### Keep a run-once backfill effect's deps empty, or it wipes live state _(proposed for this repo)_

Effects that seed a buffer which a live subscription then owns must have empty (or genuinely minimal) deps. Adding a collection the effect body doesn't read — because a render-time helper reads it — re-runs the seed on every unrelated mutation of that collection and throws away everything the subscription accumulated. Where a dep is genuinely needed, key on a derived signature of only the fields that matter and read the object through a ref.

`src/features/triggers/sub_live_stream/LiveStreamTab.tsx` documents the bug and the fix:

### Render a merged feed only down to the horizon every source loaded _(proposed for this repo)_

When a single scrollable feed k-way-merges pages from N sources, rendering everything you have lets a shallower source's older rows appear ABOVE the user's scroll position on the next page. Compute the horizon — the deepest timestamp every source has loaded past — render only at or above it, and make loadMore deepen the shallowest source.

`src/features/fleet/monitor/channels/useLensFeed.ts`:

> "Cross-team paging is a k-way merge, so the visible rows stop at the HORIZON — the deepest timestamp every team has provably loaded past. Rendering below it would let a shallower team's rows appear ABOVE the user's scroll position on the next page. `loadMore` deepens the shallowest team, which is exactly what raises the horizon."

```ts
flat.sort((a, b) => b.item.at.localeCompare(a.item.at) || b.item.id.localeCompare(a.item.id));
const horizon = mergeHorizon(states);
const visible = horizon === null ? flat : flat.filter((r) => r.item.at >= horizon);
return {
  rows: visible,
  loading: states.length === 0 || states.some((s) => !s.loaded),
  hasMore: states.some((s) => !s.exhausted) || visible.length < flat.length,
};
```

Two supporting invariants in the same file:
- **The client comparator must match the server's ranking exactly.** "Same comparator the server ranks by — (at, id) desc. The merge must sort identically or paging would interleave wrongly." Note the `id` tiebreak — timestamp alone is not a total order.
- **`hasMore` is two conditions**: an unexhausted source, *or* loaded-but-hidden rows behind the horizon.

### Tear down subscriptions on re-entry, and store the listen promise _(proposed for this repo)_

Two subscription leaks recur with async `listen()` APIs. Re-entering a start path overwrites the stored unlisten set, orphaning the previous subscriptions forever with nothing able to reach them — so tear down before subscribing again, and filter every handler by the job id it belongs to. ## integration

### Gate an integration by config, and fail closed on network errors _(proposed for this repo)_

An integration that silently falls back to a heuristic whenever the network fails cannot be distinguished, in production, from one that is working. Gate it on an explicit enablement check, have the real and fallback paths produce the same outcome union so callers never fork on source, and give a genuine network failure its own unavailable variant instead of quietly degrading.

docs/CULTURE.md 'External API integration' convention, mirroring src/lib/citations/verify.ts: `isCourtListenerEnabled()` checks `COURTLISTENER_DISABLED==="true"` first (always forces heuristic for offline tests), then `COURTLISTENER_API_TOKEN` presence. `LookupOutcome` (src/lib/citations/types.ts:194-202) is the single union both `courtlistener.ts` and the heuristic path produce, with a `{kind:"unavailable"; reason}` variant explicitly not the same as a silent heuristic fallback. Rule stated verbatim: 'Network errors return a typed unavailable variant. Never silently fall back to heuristic in production behavior — fail closed and surface the error.'

### Generate the API contract from the live handlers _(proposed for this repo)_

Hand-maintained type bindings between a server and its clients drift the moment a handler changes without its annotation. Generate the contract document from the live handlers and the structs they actually serialize, then generate the client's types from that document, so there is one artifact to keep honest instead of one per type.

`crates/brainiac-server/src/openapi.rs:1-8` — doc comment states the no-drift guarantee explicitly; `console/package.json:12` `"gen:api": "openapi-typescript ../openapi.json -o src/lib/api-schema.d.ts"`. This differs from Personas' own ts-rs-per-struct pattern (`TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` writing to `src/lib/bindings/`) — brainiac's approach centralizes the contract in one generated document instead of one file per Rust type.

### Escalate to a costlier fetch tier only on evidence of failure _(proposed for this repo)_

When several fetch strategies differ by an order of magnitude in cost, run the cheapest first and climb only on evidence — a measurably thin body, a bot-wall marker, an error — never on a guess. Derive the escalation decision from a structured verdict rather than matching strings, and remember per host which tier keeps losing so the ladder gets cheaper over time.

`crates/core/src/fetcher.rs:1-8` module doc lays out the ladder explicitly. `CHALLENGE_MARKERS` (lines 24-34) is a small, deliberately conservative bot-wall keyword list scanned only over the first 4096 chars (`CHALLENGE_SCAN_CHARS`, line 38) for cheap interstitial detection. `FetchStrategy` enum (`Http`/`Browser`/`Auto`/`AutoWithResearch`, lines 42-52) with `Auto` as `#[default]`. `AppContext::fetch` (app.rs:194-298) consults `crate::tiers::TierMemory::preferred(host)` to skip the HTTP tier for hosts with a learned pattern of loss, and calls `learn_tier` after every outcome to keep training it — `http_lost` is derived from the structured `TierVerdict` enum (Thin/Blocked/Error), not string matching on the trace text (app.rs:277-287).

### Collapse an unrecognized status to unknown, never to green _(proposed for this repo)_

A dashboard merging lifecycle status from heterogeneous backends will meet strings it does not know, and the default it picks decides whether it lies optimistically or pessimistically. Define the status union as a documented contract, map every source through a named total mapper, collapse unrecognized or unconfirmable values to a neutral unknown, and forbid folding real failures into that neutral value.

`src/features/agents/sub_deployment/components/deploymentTypes.ts` writes the contract into the type's doc comment, variant by variant, and closes with a prohibition:

```ts
 * - `unknown` — the source status string did not match any known variant,
 *   OR a live GitLab probe could not confirm the deployment's state
 *   (API unreachable). ... **Authors MUST NOT collapse "deployment is broken"
 *   or "heartbeat missing" into `unknown` — those are `failed`. Reserve
 *   `unknown` for unrecognized strings or unconfirmable probes.**
export type DeployStatus = 'active' | 'paused' | 'failed' | 'file-based' | 'unknown';
```

Both mappers are total and fail neutral:

```ts
export function mapCloudStatus(raw: string | null | undefined): DeployStatus {
  if (raw === 'active' || raw === 'paused' || raw === 'failed') return raw;
  return 'unknown';
}
// "...reconciles the live Duo Agent registry against deployment history — so a
//  crashed/removed agent no longer renders a false green `active`."
export function mapGitlabStatus(raw: string | null | undefined): DeployStatus {
  if (raw && GITLAB_STATUS_TOKENS.has(raw as DeployStatus)) return raw as DeployStatus;
  return 'unknown';
}
``

### Report whether the cache answered from freshness or from rescue _(proposed for this repo)_

A cache that silently rescues a failed network call hides a broken live channel behind fresh-looking content. Have the fetch layer return the provenance of the payload and map it to distinct statuses, so served-because-still-fresh and served-because-the-network-died are separable — and surface the degraded one in the UI, not only in telemetry.

`src/features/home/sub_releases/useLiveRoadmap.ts` documents the ladder up front:

```
 * `fresh`       — payload came from the network this session.
 * `cached`      — disk cache was still fresh enough to skip the network. Healthy path.
 * `stale`       — disk cache used as a *rescue* because the network attempt failed.
 *                 Degraded path — the live channel is silently broken.
 * `unavailable` — no cache AND network failed. Caller falls back to bundled roadmap content.
```

```ts
function statusFromSource(source: LiveRoadmapSource) {
  switch (source) { case 'network': return 'fresh'; case 'cache': return 'cached'; case 'stale': return 'stale'; }
}
// and a failure never clobbers already-good data:
if (!result) setStatus((prev) => (prev === 'loading' ? 'unavailable' : prev));
```

The status is rendered as a pill (`LiveRoadmapStatusPill.tsx`), so degradation is visible to the user rather than only to telemetry.

### Demote an unknown enum value visibly, with a breadcrumb _(proposed for this repo)_

A shipped client will meet content authored by a newer server, and dropping the values it does not recognize makes the omission invisible. Coerce each unknown value to the safest known member — a visible demotion, not a disappearance — leave a telemetry breadcrumb naming the raw value and the item so schema drift is observable, and de-duplicate ids the server may ship twice.

`src/features/home/sub_releases/roadmapItems.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Narrow a server-supplied status to one this build knows. Unknown -> 'planned'
 * (a visible demotion, not a drop) with a Sentry breadcrumb so schema drift is
 * observable. Same forward-compat policy for narrowPriority -> 'later'.
 */
function narrowStatus(raw, itemId) {
  if (raw && KNOWN_STATUSES.has(raw)) return raw;
  if (raw) Sentry.addBreadcrumb({ category: 'live-roadmap', message: `narrowStatus: unknown value '${raw}' coerced to 'planned'`, data: { itemId } });
  return 'planned';
}
function dedupeById(items) { /* keeps first, breadcrumbs the drop at level 'warning' */ }
```

The module docstring also pins the content-level rule: *"a schema-valid but content-empty live payload must not blank the roadmap"* — the bundled content is the floor. The registry equivalent is in `src/features/home/sub_cockpit/CockpitPanel.tsx`, where a widget `kind` with no entry in `cockpitWidgetRegistry` renders a bordered `unknown_widget` cell instead of throwing or rendering nothing.

### Defend a flaky embed against errors, stalls and repeat failures _(proposed for this repo)_

A third-party player or widget fails in three distinct ways and each needs its own defence: it errors, so separate fatal from transient; it stalls silently, so arm a watchdog on every start and treat the timeout as a failure; and it fails repeatedly, so memoize failures for the session and cap consecutive auto-skips. Wrap the vendor SDK so every method is caught and the whole surface degrades to no-ops.

`src/features/plugins/radio/components/RadioFooter.tsx:130-144`:

> Session blacklist of YouTube video IDs that have failed this run — either via a fatal `onError` (100/101/150/etc.) or via the silent-stall watchdog. … `skipBudgetRef` caps consecutive blacklist-skips so an entirely broken station can't loop forever — it resets on station change and on every successful PLAYING state.

Supporting pieces in the same file: a cheap up-front id-format check (`YT_VIDEO_ID_RE`, `:66-76`) "to avoid a 1-2s round trip"; an 8s watchdog armed per start (`armWatchdog`, `:179-190`) that blacklists the stalled id on fire (`:334-342`); and `isFatalYouTubeError` (`:59-64`) separating fatal from transient.

`radio/hooks/useYouTubePlayer.ts:137-166` wraps every SDK method in try/catch so the surface degrades to no-ops, and `:110-113` records a host-specific workaround worth knowing: a reduced-tracking embed host is used because the standard one's ad/analytics scripts throw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'plugins')" inside Tauri's WebView2.

The render-time analogue is `artist/sub_gallery/ThreeViewer.tsx:99-116` — a class error boundary specifically because Drei's `useGLTF` turns

A protocol carried over a fire-and-forget event channel strands every pending request on a client reload. Fetch a snapshot on mount, subscribe to live events, and dedupe by request id inside the reducer so the snapshot/live race is impossible by construction rather than by ordering luck — and where a restored request has lost its payload, label the degraded value instead of fabricating one.

```

## llm

### Funnel every model call through one provider-agnostic function _(proposed for this repo)_

Feature code that imports a provider SDK directly spreads model configuration, caching and failure handling across every route. Route all generation through a single provider-agnostic function that resolves the provider from the environment, applies the response cache, and returns a null-shaped result callers treat as 'use the deterministic fallback' rather than an exception to catch ad hoc.

`src/lib/ai/index.ts:29-51` — `generateText` checks `getCachedText`, dynamically imports `./provider-claude` or `./provider-gemini`, and caches only non-null replies. Comment: "Provider-agnostic LLM text generation. One seam — `generateText` — used by every AI route". Consumers (`src/lib/ai/ledger-agent.ts`, `narrative.ts`) inject this function rather than importing a provider directly, matching a `ConciergeProvider`/`NarrativeProvider` interface for testability.

### Verify model output against a server-built fact digest _(proposed for this repo)_

Telling a model to use only the figures you supplied reduces fabrication but does not prevent it. Build the fact digest server-side from deterministic tools, then check the reply afterwards: any number absent from the digest means the whole answer is discarded and the deterministic fallback ships instead. The prompt asks; the post-hoc check enforces.

`src/lib/ai/ledger-agent.ts:108-123`: "Enforce grounding (Tiger P0-6): ... any $ or % figure in the answer that doesn't appear in the digest is fabricated. Reject it → /api/ask falls back to the deterministic answerLocally router rather than ship an invented number. (The prompt only ASKS the model to stay grounded; this enforces it.)" Also treats conversation history and the user question as untrusted JSON-encoded data inside the prompt (prompt-injection defense), see lines 64, 79, 85.

### Ban provider SDK imports outside the call seam with a lint rule _(proposed for this repo)_

A documented 'always call through our wrapper' rule is invisible to the fortieth route someone adds later. Make the boundary physical: a restricted-import rule that rejects the provider SDK everywhere except the seam directory, so a bypass fails lint instead of relying on review. The seam itself stays a dispatcher over interchangeable engines.

`eslint.config.js` (repo root) adds a scoped rule: `files: ["**/*.{ts,tsx}"], ignores: ["src/lib/ai/**"]` with `no-restricted-imports` on `@google/generative-ai` pointing to `docs/CULTURE.md §2`. `callAI.ts:1-16` states the doctrine in a header comment and is itself a dispatcher over interchangeable provider engines (`gemini` prod default, `claude-cli` dev/test, `mock` for UAT) selected via `AI_PROVIDER`. A grep for `generative-ai` outside `src/lib/ai/` returns zero hits, confirming the rule holds in practice, not just on paper.

### Keep providers dumb; put cross-cutting AI concerns in the dispatcher _(proposed for this repo)_

If each provider implements its own cost ceiling, empty-response detection, quality gating and logging, the engines drift and every caller must know which one it got. Let a provider do only the raw call and its error mapping, and give the dispatcher every shared post-processing step, so all engines behave identically at the call site.

src/lib/ai/callAI.ts:112-336 runs, in order: multimodal-capability guard (147-162), billing-scoped provider call (171-198), provider-error logging (200-218), post-hoc cost-ceiling check (228-250, deliberately post-hoc since cost is only known after billing — see AICallRequest.maxCostUsd comment in types.ts:38-48), empty/blank-content guard using TRIMMED text (252-281), self-grading quality layer for legal purposes (283-291), and an optional hard quality gate via `minQualityScore` (293-320) that returns a typed `quality_blocked` error instead of unsafe text. types.ts:132-134 states explicitly: providers 'do NOT log, apply the cost ceiling, or check for empty output — the dispatcher owns that shared post-processing so both engines behave identically.'

### Refuse silent cross-provider fallback on a money-critical path _(proposed for this repo)_

Silently switching engines when the configured one fails hides a misconfiguration exactly where it costs most. When a provider is explicitly forced, return that engine or nothing and never the alternate, so the failure surfaces loudly; apply shared concerns such as response caching as a wrapper around whichever engine was chosen so the decision does not change behaviour elsewhere.

`src/lib/llm/index.ts:1-52`: "A forced provider returns that engine or null — NEVER the alternate. A silent cross-fall (e.g. Gemini key rotated → Claude CLI runs) would hide a misconfiguration on the money/billing path, so surface it loudly instead." The chosen provider is then wrapped in `withResponseCache()` (an input-hash response cache) as a decorator, so caching is applied uniformly regardless of which provider is active, and the wrapper is rebuilt fresh per call but shares one module-level cache singleton.

### Bind a provider per pipeline stage behind one chat trait _(proposed for this repo)_

Different stages of a pipeline have different quality needs, so one global model choice either overpays everywhere or underperforms where it matters. Define one narrow chat trait, implement it once per provider family (a single OpenAI-compatible implementation covers many by base-URL swap), and let a router hold a provider per named stage so model choice becomes central configuration rather than call-site code.

`crates/brainiac-gateway/src/lib.rs:1-100` — trait at `:64-68`, `Stage` enum at `:75-100` with per-stage rationale ("Extraction wants the strongest model; resolution/contradiction... a cheaper model is usually enough"). All providers ride the same shared `resilience` + `lighttrack` telemetry path (`:1-4`).

### Fuse heterogeneous retrievers by rank, not by normalized score _(proposed for this repo)_

Lexical, semantic and graph retrievers produce scores on incomparable scales, so any cross-retriever normalization is a guess dressed as arithmetic. Fuse on rank instead, with an optional weight toward the lexical list for identifier-heavy queries, and keep tie-breaks deterministic so the same inputs always yield the same ordering.

`crates/brainiac-core/src/fusion.rs:1-60` — doc at `:1-5` ("RRF is deliberately the only fusion strategy in v0"), `reciprocal_rank_fusion` and `weighted_reciprocal_rank_fusion` both deterministic (stable tie-break by first-appearance order).

### Strip forged delimiters from untrusted text in one shared helper _(proposed for this repo)_

Third-party text fenced into a prompt can close its own fence and continue as instructions. Sanitize every untrusted blob through one provider-neutral helper that removes any copy of the chosen delimiter before embedding, keep it shared by every prompt path so a hardening change cannot land on one path and not the other, and record the residual gaps honestly instead of implying the problem is closed.

`promptSafety.ts:1-26`: kept deliberately provider-neutral ("Kept here ... as the single source of truth so a hardening change can't silently apply to one prompt path but not the other") and reused by both the draft builder (ai-gemini) and the deep-fit builder (match-engine). The module also documents its own residual gap honestly: "Whitespace/Unicode variants remain a residual gap — a random per-request nonce delimiter is the gold-standard follow-up" — an example of the codebase flagging known limits rather than overclaiming safety. Covered by `src/lib/llm/injection.test.ts`.

### Keep provider selection pure and gate per-request overrides _(proposed for this repo)_

Provider choice that lives inside the SDK-loading code cannot be unit tested without loading an SDK or spawning a subprocess. Resolve it in a pure string-parsing module, and if a per-request header may override the environment choice, put that behind an explicit off-by-default flag — otherwise a client can force a production deploy into an engine that was only ever meant for local development.

`select.ts:28-36`: "OFF by default: the header is a local dev/testing affordance, and claude-cli spawns a local `claude` child process (shell:true on Windows), so a production deploy must NOT let a client flip the backend per request. The LLM types contract says claude-cli is 'never in production' — this is the code that enforces it." This is a concrete instance of "contract enforced in code, not just docs."

### Make a metered AI route a spec object, not hand-rolled pipeline code _(proposed for this repo)_

Every charged AI route repeats the same sequence — parse, rate-limit, charge, call, guard, persist, respond — and every hand-rolled copy gets one of the ordering invariants wrong. Own the pipeline once and let a route declare only its own parse, prompt, guard and persist hooks, so rules like 'rate-limit before charge' and 'a reclaimed charge is never billed' hold by construction.

`src/lib/ai/operation.ts:23-56` docstring names the exact pipeline and the 4 cross-cutting invariants it owns: (1) DISCLAIMER present on every error body, (2) rate-limit strictly before charge, charge strictly before model call, (3) a model throw OR unusable guard output reclaims the charge and falls back to a mock labelled `source:'mock'` (a mock is NEVER billed), (4) persist is best-effort and never fails a paid response. Backs 8 specs: qualify, draft, rfe, guidance, evidence/categorize, rfe/forecast, draft/critique, qualify/best-path (verified via grep — exactly these 8 files import `executeAiOperation`; every other API route is legitimately non-AI, e.g. checkout/health/session/export).

### Apply guardrails and telemetry as decorators built once at the seam _(proposed for this repo)_

Cross-cutting behaviour written inside each engine drifts, and the drift is silent — one engine stops reporting errors and nobody notices for months. Expose one minimal generate interface, layer guardrails and cost/latency telemetry as decorators applied once at construction, and state what each layer deliberately does not do so it cannot creep into responsibilities that belong per-route.

`src/lib/llm/guards.ts:1-27` docstring explains guards are deliberately NON-BLOCKING/observability-only — JSON structural validity is enforced downstream per-route by `spec.guard`+`extractJson`, not in this shared layer — an explicit contract preventing scope creep into the decorator. `src/lib/llm/client.ts:77-127` `withTelemetry` centralizes the empty-output-is-still-an-error rule and fire-and-forget `trackLlm` emission for BOTH engines, called out as fixing a real prior drift ('the drift that once let the Gemini path drop its error events while Claude reported them'). `getLlm({requiresImages:true})` at line 50 structurally excludes the Claude CLI engine for multimodal ops.

### Separate the fallback ordering policy from provider execution _(proposed for this repo)_

Fallback logic entangled with SDK loading can only be tested with network mocks, so in practice it is not tested at all. Express candidate ordering as a pure function of engine availability plus preference, with development-only engines last, keep invocation and telemetry outside it, and terminate the list in a deterministic template so a keyless build still produces something.

`src/lib/llm/router.ts:1-33` — "Pure + dependency-free so it's gate-testable and shared by getLlm() and any future cascade. The actual provider load + per-call telemetry stay in index.ts." Falls back to a deterministic template when the candidate list is empty (keyless build).

### Write output quality gates as pure functions shared by CI and replay _(proposed for this repo)_

A gate that exists only inside a test cannot check production output, and a runtime check cannot tell you that a prompt edit made things worse. Define pass/warn/fail gates as I/O-free functions over prompt construction, fallback templates and live output, then run the identical functions from CI, from a local verbose runner, and over replayed production traces.

`src/lib/llm/gates.ts:1-18` doc: "No I/O and no SDK import here, so this module is shared by the CI gate test and the verbose runner, and the live model call lives only in the runner." `liveGates()` (line 302) re-parses real/replayed model output with the same parser production uses and includes prompt-injection guard checks (`INJECTION_RE`, `promptGuardsUntrafcted`) as hard-fail gates, not just style checks. `package.json` scripts: `llm:gate`, `eval:replay`.

### Load providers lazily and order the seam decorators deliberately _(proposed for this repo)_

Importing every provider SDK at the seam drags all of them into the bundle and couples the app to engines it will never select. Import the chosen provider lazily, and treat decorator order as load-bearing: tracing outermost so cache hits still emit a trace, cache innermost so identical retries skip the round-trip, with trace flushes scheduled off the request path so a billed call never waits on telemetry.

`src/lib/llm/index.ts:88-139`: `llmProviderId()` gates `claude-cli`/`mock` to non-production (`claudeCliAllowed()`), `getLlm()` returns `null` when Gemini has no API key (routes must handle offline fallback), and providers are `await import(...)`-ed so neither the Gemini SDK nor `child_process` enters a bundle unless selected. Decorator order is explicit and load-bearing: `withTracing(withCache(await load(id)))` — tracing outermost so cache hits still emit a fast trace; cache sits just above the provider so identical retries skip the round-trip. `withTracing` (lines 36-86) schedules the Langfuse write via `scheduleAfterResponse` so a billed AI call never blocks on the trace flush.

### Wire the resilience stack to your main surface, not a side capability _(proposed for this repo)_

A provider abstraction carrying cache, rate limiting, circuit breaking and cost tracking earns nothing if the app's primary generation surface routes around it. When fallback chains exist for secondary capabilities while the main one is empty and marked deprecated, that is an unfinished migration rather than a design decision — name it as such and finish it.

`src/app/lib/ai/unified-provider.ts:50-56` — `DEFAULT_FALLBACKS` shows `'text-generation': []` explicitly deprecated in favor of CLI skills; `'vision': ['gemini']`, `'image-generation': ['leonardo']` remain wired. Consumers confirmed via grep: only `src/app/api/ai/art-style/extract/route.ts`, `evaluate-image/route.ts`, `generate-images/route.ts`, `image-extraction/gemini/route.ts` import from `@/app/lib/ai` (the barrel). Supporting modules: `cache.ts`, `circuit-breaker.ts`, `cost-tracker.ts`, `rate-limiter.ts`, `retry.ts` all live alongside it and are each independently unit-tested (`__tests__/`).

### Treat a spawned CLI as a dev or agentic engine, never the prod path _(proposed for this repo)_

Shelling out to a locally installed model CLI is legitimate for local development and for genuinely agentic, tool-using work, but it makes every deploy depend on a developer-machine binary. Put an API provider behind the same interface as the production default and keep the CLI an opt-in engine chosen by the same selector, so the two are interchangeable rather than parallel systems.

**Why this is one shared problem**

Eight members reach Claude, and the portfolio has already converged on the answer in five of them — CLI is the dev/opt-in engine, an API provider is the prod default, both behind one selector. The two that put a spawned CLI on the production path are solving the identical problem (get model output for a request) with a deployment-fragile mechanism, not a different problem.

**Current approaches**

- **ChainSonar** — The one reasoning call (curating insider wallets) shells out to the local `claude` CLI in -p --output-format json print mode over stdio and parses the CLI's JSON envelope — no API SDK anywhere.
- **studio-story** — All conversational/agentic text work spawns the Claude Code CLI per execution and streams it back over SSE; the real unified provider (cache, rate limit, circuit breaker, cost tracking) is deliberately scoped to vision/image only.
- **Grant Writing Nonprofits** — Pure SDK-free select.ts resolves LLM_PROVIDER — gemini default, claude-cli local — so provider choice is unit-testable without spawning the CLI.
- **Immigration Paperwork** — One Llm { name, generate() } interface with Gemini in prod and Claude CLI

### Make failover an explicit ordering policy with telemetry on every hop _(proposed for this repo)_

Refusing all failover and cascading silently are both wrong: one trades availability, the other hides misconfiguration on the path that costs money. Express failover as a pure, testable candidate-ordering function separated from execution and record every hop in telemetry — and treat a fallback chain that covers a secondary capability but not the primary one as an inconsistency rather than a design.

**Why this is one shared problem**

Every one of these apps has exactly one LLM chokepoint and multiple configured engines — the shared question is what happens when the chosen engine fails. The three answers in the portfolio are mutually exclusive and one of them (pure policy + telemetered execution) preserves both reliability and the operator signal the other two trade away.

**Current approaches**

- **Apprenticeship Placement** — getLlm() selects Gemini (prod) or Claude CLI (dev) and explicitly refuses to fall back from one to the other on failure.
- **Local SEO Agency** — routeCandidates() is a pure dependency-free function turning engine availability + preference into an ordered try-list (dev-only claude-cli last); invocation and per-call telemetry stay outside the policy.
- **studio-story** — A full unified provider with per-capability fallback chains, cache, rate limiter, circuit breaker and cost tracking exists — but is deliberately NOT wired to text generation, the app's primary LLM surface.
- **brainiac** — One ChatProvider trait behind Arc<dyn>, with ProviderRouter binding a provider per pipeline Stage; routing is per-stage configuration with no failover pat

### Pin every model surface with offline gates, not runtime checks alone _(proposed for this repo)_

Runtime grounding checks catch a bad answer in the moment but cannot tell you that a prompt or model change made the surface worse overall. Ship pure gate or golden-fixture functions that run identically in CI, in replay and against live output, so a regression is caught by the same assertions wherever it shows up.

**Why this is one shared problem**

Every member here ships LLM output as a core product surface, so they all face the same regression risk from a prompt or model change. Three built reusable deterministic gates; the others verify only at request time or not at all, and ChainSonar's own harvest states the absence is early-stage drift rather than a deliberate 'tests elsewhere' choice.

**Current approaches**

- **Local SEO Agency** — gates.ts holds pure, engine-agnostic pass/warn/fail functions over prompt-construction, template-fallback and live-output layers, with zero I/O, reused by the CI quality-gate test, the verbose runner and probe batteries.
- **brainiac** — A golden-fixture eval harness runs the REAL stage code per concern with unconditional hard gates (RLS leaks = 0, superseded-in-top3 = 0) plus soft baseline-relative gates.
- **ai-bookkeeper** — Verifies grounding at request time only — ungroundedFigures discards any reply containing a $/% absent from the server-built facts digest, falling back to a deterministic response; no offline gate suite.
- **ChainSonar** — Zero test files anywhere; the only verification artifact is scripts/prove-ingest.mts, a manual pro

### Serialize the form's answers into the intent so the model won't re-ask _(proposed for this repo)_

When a UI collects structured choices and then hands an intent to a model that interrogates the user for the same things, the user answers everything twice. Append a deterministic, human-readable summary of those choices to the prompt so the model's clarifying-question heuristics read them as already answered — including explicit negatives, because an omitted choice reads as unset rather than declined.

`src/features/agents/shared/quickConfig/quickConfigTypes.ts` → `serializeQuickConfig(state)` emits a `\n---\n`-delimited block (`Schedule: Weekly on Monday at 09:00`, `Services: postgres (tables: orders, users)`, `Event triggers: …`, `Delivery channels: …`). Notable calibration in that code: a table subset is annotated but "all tables" is left unannotated "so the build prompt isn't cluttered with redundant scope notes", and an *empty* channel selection is serialized as an explicit negative (`Messages: none — this persona produces no user-facing messages`) rather than omitted.

`src/features/agents/sub_glyph/useComposeConfig.tsx` `launch()` does the same for memory/review toggles, stating the intent directly: "the build prompt's heuristics open/skip those gates from the keywords, so a user who set them in the UI never re-answers them mid-build." That hook is also the reusable backbone — every compose-surface variant is "just a layout over `items` + `modals`", so visual prototypes share one config/serialization path.

### Mine your corpus for the option set and ship each option's directive _(proposed for this repo)_

Behaviour dials invented by a designer rarely match how the artifacts actually vary. Derive the option vocabulary from the corpus you already have, and store the exact prompt sentence on the same record as the label and the icon, so a user's selection compiles into a directive block mechanically and an untouched picker contributes nothing to the prompt.

`src/features/agents/sub_glyph/personaCore/catalog.ts` holds a 20-trait vocabulary across 5 axes, each entry carrying `{ id, axis, label, count, icon, blurb, directive }` — `count` is the number of personas in the 120-persona corpus exhibiting the trait (`escalates` 66, `terse` 48, `ships-fast` 5), and `directive` is the literal prompt line. The header records the finding that shaped the UI: "Character in the library lives in PROSE, not dials — only 18 of 120 personas carry numeric `core` — so discrete traits (not sliders) carry most of the personality."

`src/features/agents/sub_glyph/personaCore/usePersonaCore.ts` then compiles selection into a prompt block in `launchAugmentation()` — archetype stance, a bucketed disposition sentence, `CONFLICT_DIRECTIVE[style]`, then one `t.directive` per selected trait — returning `\n---\nPersona core:\n- …`. It returns `""` when the user never touched the controls, so an untouched picker adds nothing to the prompt. `ARCHETYPE_TRAITS` preloads dominant traits per archetype so a preset lands as a complete character.

### Compute the composite score in one module and re-export it everywhere _(proposed for this repo)_

When grids, reports, cards and detail panels each rank variants by a weighted composite, any inline re-derivation produces surfaces that disagree about which variant won. Judges time out, fail, or decline a dimension. Coercing that null to zero drags every average down and makes a broken run look like a bad model. ## observability

### Log through one closed event union, never a bare console call _(proposed for this repo)_

Make every application event a variant of one closed discriminated union, and allow exactly one logging helper in application code with a lint rule holding the line. Adding an event type then means extending the union first, so the type checker rather than review catches the branch that logs a partial row.

eslint.config.js:59-62: `"no-console": ["error", {allow: ["warn","error"]}]`, comment cites docs/CULTURE.md §6. docs/CULTURE.md principle #6: 'Adding a new event type means extending the union first — the helper is exhaustive (TypeScript catches missing variants).' callAI.ts's `emit()` closure (lines 129-141) is the canonical example: it captures invariant context once and each of 6 outcome branches passes only its delta (`AiCallDelta`, a `Pick<AICallEvent,...>` of required fields) so 'no branch can log a partial row.'

### Count the swallows inside the helper, not at the call sites _(proposed for this repo)_

When a codebase routes intentional error-swallowing through one helper, make that helper count. Aggregate swallows per call-site tag, emit a periodic rollup (one structured log + one breadcrumb), and sample a real exception capture for high-frequency tags — so a path that fails 400 times a session becomes a visible issue instead of 400 invisible breadcrumbs. Zero changes at the call sites.

`src/lib/silentFailureTelemetry.ts` sits behind `silentCatch()` / `silentCatchNull()` in `src/lib/silentCatch.ts` (250+ call sites, all untouched):

> With 250+ call sites, the aggregate swallow rate is an unmeasured failure surface — no single breadcrumb tells you "auth:refresh has failed 400 times this session".

Design constraints stated in the module header: **zero change at the 250+ call sites** (`silentCatch` calls `recordSwallow` internally), **zero user-visible effect**, and **HMR-durable state on `globalThis`** (same singleton pattern the repo uses for `executionBuffers` / `eventBus`).

Tunables are exported constants rather than magic numbers, and each one closes a specific failure mode:
```ts
export const SWALLOW_ROLLUP_MAX = 100;               // flush by volume
export const SWALLOW_ROLLUP_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 60_000; // …or by time
export const SWALLOW_ROLLUP_TOP_N = 8;               // keep the rollup readable
export const SWALLOW_SAMPLE_EVERY = 25;              // escalate a repeat offender
export const SWALLOW_SAMPLE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000; // a storm can't flood Sentry
```

### Make 'unknown' a first-class state, distinct from zero and absent _(proposed for this repo)_

Any surface that reconstructs history or aggregates several independent sources must carry an explicit unknown/stale state and render it, rather than substituting a default that reads as a measured fact. Absence of a record means the observation is missing — never that the thing succeeded, never that the count is zero.

This is the strongest cross-cutting doctrine in the execution/orchestration surface, and it is enforced by tests rather than convention.

**Scheduling history** — `src/features/schedules/libs/calendarHelpers.ts` documents the failure it replaced:

> "The calendar used to colour every past projected slot green/red from the trigger's OVERALL health, so a slot the engine SKIPPED (rate-limited, out-of-window, app closed, over budget) rendered as a confident past-success. It was asserting history it didn't have."

The `CalendarEvent.kind` union is now `'projected' | 'past-success' | 'past-failure' | 'past-unknown'`, and `past-unknown` is documented as "Never a fabricated outcome — it means 'we can't assert what happened'." `classifyRunOutcome` maps non-terminal statuses (`queued`, `running`) to `past-unknown` too — a run exists but hasn't resolved, so no outcome is claimed. In `src/features/schedules/libs/useCronPreview.ts` even a *failure to fetch* run history falls through to unknown: "History unavailable — past cron slots fall through to 'past-unknown', which is the honest state, not a fabricated outcome."

### Derive stall state from output silence when there is no heartbeat _(proposed for this repo)_

A long-running job that streams output but sends no heartbeat gives you exactly one liveness signal: the gap since the last line. Track it with graded thresholds (active → waiting → stuck), reset on any new output, and let the UI change what it offers at each level instead of showing an indeterminate spinner forever.

`src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useRunnerState.ts`:

```ts
/** How long (ms) without new output before each silence level triggers. */
const SILENCE_WAITING_MS = 60_000;
const SILENCE_STUCK_MS = 120_000;
export type SilenceLevel = 'active' | 'waiting' | 'stuck';

// Track silence: update lastOutputTime when new lines arrive
useEffect(() => {
  if (outputLines.length !== lastOutputCountRef.current) {
    lastOutputCountRef.current = outputLines.length;
    lastOutputTimeRef.current = Date.now();
    setSilenceLevel('active');
  }
}, [outputLines]);

// Poll silence level while executing (piggybacks on elapsedMs updates every 500ms)
useEffect(() => {
  if (!isExecuting || !isThisPersonasExecution) { setSilenceLevel('active'); return; }
  const gap = Date.now() - lastOutputTimeRef.current;
  if (gap >= SILENCE_STUCK_MS) setSilenceLevel('stuck');
  else if (gap >= SILENCE_WAITING_MS) setSilenceLevel('waiting');
  else setSilenceLevel('active');
}, [isExecuting, isThisPersonasExecution, elapsedMs]);
```

Note the re-use of an existing 500ms tick (`elapsedMs`) as the clock instead of adding a second interval, and `StuckExecutionGuidance.tsx` as the surface the `stuck` level unlo

### Never fabricate a trend from a single loaded window _(proposed for this repo)_

A prior-period comparison is only real if the series was actually fetched at 2x the window. Splitting one window into front-half/back-half and calling the ratio 'period-over-period change' produces noise that users act on. Enforce the invariant in one splitter that returns null when no genuine prior half exists, and let consumers omit the trend chip.

`src/features/overview/libs/computeTrends.ts` centralises the split and refuses to lie:

```ts
export function splitComparisonPeriods<T>(rows: T[], currentPeriodDays: number, compareEnabled: boolean) {
  if (!compareEnabled || rows.length === 0) return null;
  const splitIdx = Math.max(0, rows.length - currentPeriodDays);
  const previous = rows.slice(0, splitIdx);
  const current  = rows.slice(splitIdx);
  if (previous.length === 0) return null;   // no genuine prior period
  return { previous, current };
}
```
JSDoc: "Callers must therefore render NO trend rather than fabricate one from a single loaded window (the front-half/back-half heuristic that used to lie on the Home 'Runs' tile)."

`src/features/overview/sub_observability/libs/useObservabilityData.ts` still carries the disabled version with the full post-mortem:
> "the data was never fetched at 2× the window, so the percentages were statistical noise. Users reacted to phantom 'cost spiked 40%' deltas that meant nothing more than 'the second half of this week was different from the first half of this week'. Returning nulls makes the Summary cards omit the trend chips."

## performance

### Use the point lookup you already have, and read shared docs once _(proposed for this repo)_

Hot request paths accumulate two quiet costs: the same record fetched twice by two independent call chains, and a list-then-find where a keyed lookup already exists and is already tested. Neither shows up in correctness tests, and both scale with tenant size rather than with traffic. Audit hot handlers for repeated reads and collection scans, and memoise per-request reads at the seam rather than at each caller.

`docs/adr/ADR-0032-performance-scalability-hot-path-redundant-reads.md`: Gap 1 (lines 19-30) — two sequential `getScoringProfile` reads per `draft-narrative` POST, no `React.cache()` wrapper; "a 100-org deployment generates ~1000 calls, each with 2 Firestore reads instead of 1." Gap 2 (lines 32-49) — `listDrafts(500).find()` used instead of `getDraftById()` (already exported from `src/features/drafts/index.ts:27`) at two call sites; "an org with 50 submitted grants holding 50 reports would cause 25,000 Firestore doc reads across both call sites on a single report-generation pass" at consultant scale. The ADR's own considered-but-not-actioned section (lines 51-55) shows deliberate restraint elsewhere (e.g. NOT batching `upsertDraftSections`'s 3 sequential writes because that would break per-section billing tracking) — so this genuinely reads as an isolated oversight the team caught via scheduled architecture review, not a systemic anti-pattern.

### Mirror a running total in memory instead of re-aggregating per call _(proposed for this repo)_

A pre-flight check that re-aggregates a ledger costs time proportional to the history so far, which makes a single job quadratic in its own call count — invisible in a short test and crippling in a long run. Seed the total once from the ledger at start and advance it in process on every write, so the check on the hot path is arithmetic.

`crates/core/src/app.rs:128-137` — doc comment explicitly states the reason: "this is on the pre-flight path of every metered call, so a SELECT SUM here costs O(spend events so far) per call and O(n^2) over a job." `costs.rs:1-9` module doc: "[SpentTotal] mirrors a job's total in memory so the per-call budget check doesn't re-aggregate the ledger."

### Split localisation per route section and preload before mount _(proposed for this repo)_

One monolithic locale bundle is paid in full by every user for strings most of them never see, and loading it after mount produces a visible English first paint. Split each locale into per-section chunks at build time, declare which sections each route needs, warm the persisted locale and route before the app mounts under a bounded timeout, and expose the catalogue through a proxy that loads a section on first access so untouched sections never load at all.

The 500KB+ monolithic locale bundles were retired in May 2026. The pipeline, per `.claude/CLAUDE.md` → *Architecture (section-locales pipeline)*:

1. `src/i18n/locales/<lang>.json` — authoritative human-edited catalogs (English is the source).
2. `scripts/i18n/split-locales.mjs` (runs in Vite `buildStart` and via `predev`/`prebuild` codegen) splits each non-English locale into `src/i18n/section-locales/<lang>/<section>.json` and emits English sections as parse-on-demand JSON strings.
3. `useTranslation.ts` discovers sections via `import.meta.glob('./section-locales/*/*.json', { eager: false })` — each section becomes its own async chunk. `t` is a **Proxy** that triggers loading on first property access.
4. `src/i18n/routeSections.ts` declares which sections each sidebar route needs; `BASE_SECTIONS` (common, chrome, sidebar, toasts, errors, …) always preload.
5. `main.tsx` → `preloadPersistedLocaleBeforeMount()` warms the persisted locale + persisted route **before React mounts**, bounded by a 1.2s timeout — this is what removes the English-first-paint flash for non-English users.
6. `useLanguagePrefetch()` warms chunks on hover/intent in the language switcher, so a swit
