### Run one timer per cadence bucket, not one per poller _(proposed for this repo)_

Independent pollers start at different offsets, so a shared refresh interval becomes several desynchronised bursts and every downstream cost is paid once per ticker rather than once per window. Route them through one coordinator holding a timer per rounded cadence, guard each ticker against overlapping itself, isolate failures so one cannot poison the loop, pause while the document is hidden, and fire immediately on return.

`src/lib/polling/pollingCoordinator.ts` states the motivation from measurement, not theory:

> 7+ surfaces each spun their own setInterval/setTimeout to poll IPC commands ... Their first ticks fired at different offsets within a window, so a "30s refresh" produced several desynchronized IPC bursts — SQLite paid cache-warm cost multiple times and Tauri serialization happened once per ticker.

Design: buckets of `[5s, 12s, 15s, 30s, 60s]`; `pickBucket` rounds a requested interval to the nearest. Each ticker registers `fn` plus an optional `shouldRun()` predicate and a `runWhileHidden` opt-out. Details worth copying:

- `inFlight` per ticker so a slow tick never overlaps itself.
- One failing ticker is caught and routed to `silentCatch` so it "must not poison the bucket loop".
- `onVisibilityRegained()` fires eligible tickers *immediately* rather than waiting out the bucket interval — "so users don't stare at stale state".
- A bucket with zero tickers clears its timer and deletes itself.
- The instance is a `globalThis` singleton (HMR-safe) with a `__resetPollingCoordinatorForTests` hook, and a `stats()` method for diagnostics.

### Drain speculative imports one at a time, most likely first _(proposed for this repo)_

Scheduling many speculative imports at once does not spread their cost: resolving a chunk triggers a synchronous parse-and-evaluate that ignores the idle deadline, so they stack into one long main-thread block the moment the browser goes idle. Schedule the next only when the previous settles, delay the first past the most contended startup window, and order the queue by likelihood of use because later entries now warm noticeably later.

`src/lib/idlePrefetch.ts`:

> `import()` resolution triggers a synchronous, non-interruptible V8 parse+evaluate that ignores the idle deadline; scheduling all N at once (the previous behavior) let them evaluate back-to-back in one burst the moment the browser went idle (or when the 5s idle-timeout fired under load), stacking into a multi-hundred-ms main-thread block.

The fixed `pump()` schedules the next import only in the previous one's `.finally`. Supporting decisions:

- `initialDelayMs` keeps speculative work "out of the most contended startup window — the seconds right after load, where chunk evaluation showed up as ~800ms main-thread freezes in the 2026-05-25 profiling pass".
- The `requestIdleCallback` fallback uses `MessageChannel`, not `setTimeout`: "posts run as a task (not microtask), so the browser can render between scheduled callbacks. Avoids setTimeout's 4 ms clamp without blocking the microtask queue."
- Order matters and is documented: "pass the most-likely-needed chunks first, since later entries warm noticeably later under this serialized schedule".
- Failures are swallowed by design — a missed prefetch is not fatal; the real mount surfaces the error.

### Virtualise a table with spacer rows and an opted-in scroll parent _(proposed for this repo)_

Two traps make a virtualised table silently wrong: absolutely positioning rows breaks column alignment with the header, and resolving the scroll container by a generic overflow class can latch onto a horizontal scroller, so the offset never changes and nothing past the first viewport renders. Use zero-height spacer rows to simulate the off-screen range, require the caller to mark the vertical scroller explicitly, and keep a row-count threshold below which every row renders plainly.

`src/features/agents/sub_lab/components/shared/VirtualizedTableBody.tsx` encodes both, each next to the bug it fixed:

### Defer heavy below-fold subtrees behind a named priority wrapper _(proposed for this repo)_

Keeping large non-critical trees out of the first commit usually happens as a one-off timeout buried in a layout, which is untestable and gets copied without its reasoning. Make it a small wrapper that renders children at a named priority — idle, next frame, immediate — falls back to a macrotask where the idle callback is missing, and exposes a synchronous escape hatch so tests and snapshots stay deterministic.

`src/features/shared/components/layout/DeferUntilIdle.tsx` turns a one-off band-aid into a testable primitive:

> "Use it to keep heavy below-fold trees out of the initial DOM commit so the renderer doesn't hitch — particularly relevant for Tauri/WebView2, which historically hangs when too many nodes are committed at once."

> "`next-frame` — wait one `requestAnimationFrame`. **This is the original WelcomeLayout band-aid pattern, now testable.**"

```ts
/** Test-only escape hatch. When `true`, children render synchronously on
 *  mount regardless of priority. Use to keep snapshot/RTL tests stable. */
immediate?: boolean;
```

The rIC fallback is explicit (*"on legacy Safari it does not [exist], so the implementation falls back to `setTimeout(0)` — conservative but always fires in the next macrotask"*), and the contract for `fallback` is stated so nobody puts state in it: *"The `fallback` prop is rendered once ... After children mount, the fallback is unmounted; do not put state-bearing UI there."* Covered by `DeferUntilIdle.test.tsx`.

### Host app-wide background hooks in one lazy render-nothing component _(proposed for this repo)_

Global side-effect hooks drag their domain stores into whatever module happens to host them, pulling that whole dependency graph into the initial bundle. Collect them in a single component that renders nothing, lazy-load it after first paint, and require each hook to carry the reason it must run app-wide rather than inside its own page — that annotation is what stops the file becoming a dumping ground.

Each of the ten hooks carries the reason it is global rather than page-local, which is what stops the file from silently becoming a dumping ground — e.g.:

- `useGlobalAlertEvaluator()` — *"alerts previously only fired while the Observability tab was open."*

- `useAssignmentNotificationDispatcher()` — *"Fires regardless of which page is mounted so the user is reached even if they're not on the team's canvas."*

### Cache derived parses in a WeakMap keyed on the row object _(proposed for this repo)_

List rows carrying serialised columns get re-parsed on every memo re-run. Key the derived fields on the row object itself: identity is stable across re-renders and the entry is collected when a refresh replaces the row, so no eviction policy is needed. Split the cache into cheap fields computed eagerly and expensive blobs filled only on expand, with a distinct not-yet-parsed sentinel so a lazy slot is distinguishable from a real empty result.

`src/features/templates/sub_generated/gallery/cards/reviewParseCache.ts` is the reference implementation:

```ts
// WeakMap keyed by review object identity -- entries are GC'd when the
// review object is no longer referenced (e.g. after a gallery refresh).
const reviewParseCache = new WeakMap<PersonaDesignReview, CachedReviewFields>();

getCachedLightFields(review)   // connectors + flowCount, on every row render
getCachedDesignResult(review)  // the multi-KB design_result blob, only on expansion
getCachedVerification(review, verify)      // lazily computed, cached in the same entry
getCachedReadinessScore(review, compute, …) // ditto
```

The `undefined = not yet parsed` sentinel on the cached fields is what makes the lazy slots distinguishable from a real `null` result.

The same technique appears twice more, each with its own justification comment:
- `sub_generated/shared/templateComplexity.ts` — `signalsCache` because "gallery filter passes call computeDifficulty / computeSetupLevel per template per memo re-run, and each extraction JSON.parses four fields (including the multi-KB design_result blob). Review objects are identity-stable across memo re-runs, so a WeakMap keyed

### Give every background poller three ways to stop _(proposed for this repo)_

A poll that reads its target id from persisted storage and swallows its errors will poll a session the backend has already collected, forever, and replay stale notifications into the next session. It needs a consecutive-failure budget that clears the stored id, an explicit clear on every terminal status, and a clear on malformed stored data — with non-terminal statuses distinguished so a resumable flow is not discarded along with the dead ones.

`src/features/templates/sub_generated/gallery/cards/useAdoptionCompletionNotifier.ts` polls a background adoption every 5s while the modal is closed. The failure budget carries the incident in its comment:

```ts
/** After this many consecutive snapshot fetch failures, clear the localStorage
 *  entry and stop polling — the backend has likely GC'd or restarted and the
 *  adoptId is dead. Without this, the empty catch silently burned CPU on a
 *  dead session indefinitely. */
const MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 5;
```

And the clear helper enumerates all three reasons it exists:

```ts
/** Discard the persisted adoption context so:
 *  - a new login session doesn't replay this adoptId for a different user
 *  - terminal notifications don't fire repeatedly for the same adoption
 *  - dead/GC'd backend snapshots stop being polled */
```

Terminal vs non-terminal is handled explicitly: `completed` and `failed` notify then clear; `awaiting_answers` notifies but keeps the entry, with the reason inline — "'awaiting_answers' is not terminal — leave the entry so the user returning to the modal can resume." A malformed localStorage payload clears itself "so we don't keep tripping the par

### Prefetch route chunks on pointer intent through one cached helper _(proposed for this repo)_

Speculative chunk loading belongs in one module where each prefetcher is memoised after its first call and a rejection resets its entry, so a failed prefetch is not permanently remembered as loaded. Fire them from real intent — pointer enter, focus, pointer down — and from idle once the landing surface has mounted. Duplicating the router's lazy imports is the one maintenance cost to accept knowingly.

`src/features/home/lib/prefetch.ts` is the whole contract:

```ts
function cache(fn: Prefetcher): Prefetcher {
  let pending: Promise<unknown> | null = null;
  return () => {
    if (!pending) pending = fn().catch((err) => {
      silentCatch('home/prefetch:chunkPrefetch')(err);
      pending = null;   // treat the chunk as still-absent; real navigation retries
    });
    return pending;
  };
}
const NAV_PREFETCHERS: Record<string, Prefetcher> = { overview: cache(() => import(...)), ... };
export function schedulePrefetchOtherHomeTabs() { return schedule(() => { ... }); }
// schedule() = requestIdleCallback({timeout: 2000}) with a setTimeout(300) fallback
```

Call sites: `NavigationGrid.tsx` `onPointerEnter={() => prefetchNavTarget(card.id)}`; `HomeWelcome.tsx` `useEffect(() => schedulePrefetchOtherHomeTabs(), [])`; `LanguageSwitcher.tsx` uses the same intent ladder for locale chunks (`onMouseEnter`/`onFocus` → `prefetchWithIntent`, `onPointerDown` → `prefetchNow`, `onMouseLeave`/`onBlur` → `cancelPrefetch`). The `NAV_PREFETCHERS` map is documented as mirroring the router's own lazy imports — that duplication is the one maintenance cost to accept.

### Choose a mount policy per tab surface instead of remounting _(proposed for this repo)_

Keying a tab container on the active tab throws away and re-runs every tab's mount work on each switch. Decide deliberately instead: cheap-but-hot tabs stay mounted and are hidden, heavy tabs mount lazily and unmount after an idle timeout so memory returns while the module stays cached and re-entry is synchronous. Either way, mount only tabs the user actually visited, and validate a persisted tab id before rendering it.

Both policies live in this scope, each with its rationale in code.

Keep-alive — `src/features/home/components/HomePage.tsx`:

```tsx
// Renders its children mounted while it's a visited tab, hiding (not unmounting)
// the inactive ones. This replaces the old key={homeTab} remount, which threw away
// and re-ran each tab's mount work on every switch — most painfully Welcome
// (nav-status fetches, fleet metrics, deferred-node commit).
const visitedRef = useRef<Set<HomeTab>>(new Set());
visitedRef.current.add(activeTab);   // only visited tabs enter the tree
```

Idle-unmount — `src/features/settings/components/SettingsPage.tsx`:

```ts
const IDLE_UNMOUNT_MS = 30_000;
const SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000;
// The lazy() module stays cached, so re-entering an unmounted tab re-mounts synchronously.
```

`HomePage` also validates the persisted tab id against a known set and falls back to Welcome, so stale persisted state can't render a dev-only or removed tab.

A panel whose data lives in local component state starts genuinely cold on every remount, so a lazy route re-ghosts every time the user returns to it. Stash the last successful fetch at module scope keyed by the entity, seed state from it, and still run the fetch to replace it silently — the skeleton then appears only on a true first-ever visit. Invalidate on the mutation that changes the numbers.

When one source in an aggregate is far slower than the rest, letting it gate first paint makes the whole surface as slow as its worst input. Publish a sequence of self-consistent frames as sources resolve, with the slower fields falling back to their documented heuristic rather than rendering blank. Guard the degraded early frame so it only paints when nothing real is on screen — painting it over cached data is a regression, not progress.

### A worker is only usable if its client handles every degenerate case _(proposed for this repo)_

Moving pure computation off the main thread is the easy half; the client around the worker is the actual pattern. Correlate requests by id, cache by content hash, stream partial results so the UI fills progressively, treat cancellation as dropping the pending entry, reject all pending work and reset the singleton on a crash so it can be lazily rebuilt, and run the same pure function inline when the worker cannot be constructed.

```ts
function hashContent(value: string | null): string {
  let hash = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i += 1) { hash ^= text.charCodeAt(i); hash = Math.imul(hash, 0x01000193); }

if (!activeWorker) { const result = diffLines(…); lineCache.set(key, result); queueMicrotask(() => onChunk(result)); … }

### Flatten a grouped list into one indexed sequence in a pure module _(proposed for this repo)_

A virtualiser only knows how to window a flat index range, so a two-level grouped list must be collapsed into a single ordered sequence of tagged items. Do the collapse in a pure dependency-free module so the index arithmetic is testable without a DOM, carry on each item the presentational adjacency facts the flat sequence would otherwise lose, and keep a threshold below which the plain markup renders verbatim.

`src/features/schedules/libs/scheduleListItems.ts` carries both the reasoning and the measurement:

```
The grouped timeline renders time-window buckets ("Overdue", "Next hour", …) each holding
N rich `ScheduleRow`s. Unwindowed that is one DOM subtree per agent (~5,100 nodes at ~70
cron agents, measured in the 2026-05-30 perf walk), and it grows linearly with the agent count.

Windowing a *grouped* list requires collapsing the two-level structure (groups → entries)
into ONE ordered sequence of rows, because a virtualizer only knows how to window a flat
index range. That collapse is this module — a pure function, so the index math is testable
without a DOM.
```

The item union carries the presentational adjacency facts the flat sequence would otherwise lose:

```ts
export type ScheduleListItem =
  | { kind: 'header'; key: string; label: string; count: number;
      /** True for the first header in the sequence — it gets no top spacing. */ first: boolean }
  | { kind: 'row'; key: string; entry: ScheduleEntry; groupLabel: string;
      /** True for the last row of its group — it gets no bottom gap. */ lastInGroup: boolean };
```

### Bound media caches by bytes, and dedupe loads through an in-flight map _(proposed for this repo)_

An entry-count cap on decoded media is not a memory bound — a few hundred full-resolution images pin gigabytes. Track accumulated bytes, evict against a byte budget, never evict the entry just inserted, and release oversized entries when their last on-screen consumer unmounts. Separately, key in-flight loads by identity so simultaneous consumers cost one decode, and export an explicit invalidation so a path reused after a delete or rename cannot serve the old bytes.

### Free decoded media with the same observer that allocated it _(proposed for this repo)_

Object URLs and media elements should be created and released by one visibility observer, so a large collection never holds more than its visible window. And any decode pipeline must tear its element down in a finally: cleanup written at the end of the success path leaks a detached element with its source still attached on every codec error or cancellation, holding the file open and its buffers resident.

For heavyweight per-item resources like terminals, sockets or decoders, make the component a mount point and keep the instance in a module-level registry keyed by id so it survives unmount. ### Gate polls on visibility, one owner, and the job still being alive _(proposed for this repo)_

Three independent gates make polling cost nothing when nobody is looking: skip while the document is hidden and re-run immediately on return, let exactly one always-mounted call site own the interval so the poll is not multiplied by however many components mounted, and stop entirely when the thing polled is inactive. Justify the cadence against the upstream's own refresh rate rather than picking a round number.

`src/features/plugins/fleet/useFleetOrphanScan.ts:25-29`:

`src/features/plugins/fleet/useFleetDebugLog.ts:22-25, 72-74`:
> Pass `poll: true` at exactly one always-mounted call site (the footer) to run the single status poll while a recording is active … so an idle fleet does no background work.

The same file explains why the controller is shared rather than component-local: the surface that starts a recording unmounts, and "an armed recorder would be stranded with no way to turn it off" (`:14-20`).

Cadence justification: `radio/hooks/useSomafmMetadata.ts:6-9` — "SomaFM updates their JSON every ~30s so anything faster wastes IPC + network without finer track resolution." `gitlab/components/GitLabPipelineViewer.tsx:59-62` gates a shared visibility-aware `usePolling` on `isRunning`. And `radio/components/RadioFooter.tsx:478-498` decouples UI cadence from persistence cadence, writing position back only every Nth tick (`POSITION_REPORT_EVERY_N_TICKS = 5`).

### Keep frame-rate values in refs, and coalesce stream deltas per frame _(proposed for this repo)_

Anything updating at animation-frame rate — a playhead, an audio level, token deltas — must not pass through component state; a re-render per tick is the failure mode. Keep the authoritative value in a ref and let consumers subscribe and touch the DOM, buffer inbound stream deltas and flush once per frame, and force a flush before any terminal transition. Commit ref writes in a layout effect, never in the render body: a speculative render that is discarded leaves callbacks reading a thrown-away value.

## process

### End every decision record with what this increment must not touch _(proposed for this repo)_

Small numbered decision records keep structural change reviewable, but the reusable half is the closing fence: an explicit out-of-scope list naming the files and behaviours the change must not affect. It is what keeps an agent-driven or unfamiliar increment narrow, and it turns the review question from a matter of taste into something checkable against the diff.

Both `docs/adr/ADR-010-typed-operation-registry.md:72-80` and `docs/adr/ADR-006-with-charged-operation-wrapper.md:80-84` end with this fencing pattern, e.g. ADR-010: 'Out of scope this increment (do NOT touch): The ledger/charge/reclaim internals... Adding new operations, or wiring the registry into UI/cost-display surfaces.' This is a deliberate scoping discipline, not incidental — visible across many ADR files with consistent structure (Context/Decision/Consequences/Out-of-scope).

### Turn every repeated review comment into a local lint rule _(proposed for this repo)_

Conventions a reviewer keeps restating — raw utility classes that have token equivalents, hand-rolled modal backdrops, direct clipboard calls, whole-store subscriptions — belong in the linter, not the checklist. Ship a rule at warning level while its migration is in flight and at error level once the invariant is absolute, so the severity itself documents which conventions are negotiable and which are not.

`eslint.config.js` registers **20 hand-written rules** under a `custom` plugin, loaded from `eslint-rules/`:

| Class | Rules |
|---|---|
| Design tokens | `no-raw-text-classes`, `no-raw-radius-classes`, `no-raw-shadow-classes`, `no-raw-spacing-classes`, `no-direct-white-colors`, `no-low-contrast-text-classes`, `no-unprefixed-wide-min-width` |
| Shared primitives | `enforce-base-modal`, `prefer-shared-clipboard`, `prefer-numeric`, `prefer-status-badge`, `prefer-section-card` |
| a11y / motion | `role-button-requires-keydown` (**error**), `enforce-reduced-motion-fallback` |
| Correctness | `no-silent-catch` (**error**), `no-loose-event-payload` (**error**), `no-unmanaged-effect-resources`, `no-whole-store-subscription`, `async-catch-requires-helper` |
| i18n | `no-hardcoded-jsx-text` |

Severity carries meaning: the three **errors** are invariants (never swallow silently, never ship an untyped event payload, never make a `role="button"` unreachable by keyboard); the warns are known incremental migrations with a documented baseline (~10k warnings, "fix-as-you-touch, do not bulk-migrate").

### Give a sprawling feature folder an owns / does NOT own table _(proposed for this repo)_

When one feature grows into many sibling modules, a co-located map naming per module both what it owns and what it explicitly does not is what actually stops duplication — the positive column alone is just a directory listing. Add the rule for where cross-module helpers go, record the intentional exceptions to the naming convention, and require the new row in the same change that creates the folder.

`src/features/agents/AGENTS.md` is a one-page table over the `sub_<concern>/` modules with `Owns` / `Does NOT own` columns — e.g. `sub_connectors` owns agent↔connector bindings but NOT credential storage (`features/vault`); `sub_model_config` owns the per-agent model profile but NOT the global one; `sub_editor` owns the shell, tab bar and draft save/restore but "Any single-tab content". It states the reason it exists: "The convention is implicit in the directory layout but was previously undocumented, causing duplicated logic across closely-related sub-modules."

It also documents the one intentional exception (`health/` is not `sub_health/` because its scoring feeds surfaces outside the editor), gives the placement rule for shared helpers (`features/agents/libs/` or `features/shared/`, "NOT inside either `sub_` dir"), and closes with a 3-step checklist for adding a module whose last step is "Add an entry to this table in the same PR that creates the folder."

### Prototype visual variants against one shared data-and-actions hook _(proposed for this repo)_

When several directions for the same surface are explored in parallel, extract the fetch, derivation and mutation handlers into one hook first. Each variant then owns only filters and layout, the comparison stays honest because behaviour is identical across them, and consolidating the winner becomes a deletion rather than a rewrite. The view model outlives the throwaway fixtures that first shaped it.

Each variant provides its own filters and layout — the hook keeps data and actions consistent across variants so we don't duplicate ~150 lines of state glue three times while prototyping."

It exports its own inferred type so variants stay in lockstep with it: `export type RoutingState = ReturnType<typeof useRoutingState>;`

## security

### Keep secret handling in one trusted process, gated explicitly _(proposed for this repo)_

Inject and consume secrets entirely inside the trusted process so plaintext never reaches the renderer, and make every exception to a trust-sensitive gate declarative and reviewable rather than a per-call decision. The layer is only as strong as its narrowest gate, and being inside the trusted process is not by itself an argument that a surface can go unauthenticated.

**Practiced here:**
- Plaintext never crosses to the renderer — secrets are injected and consumed in-process — engine · commands/credentials
- Secret-name backstop overrides a mis-authored connector schema that would downgrade a real secret to plaintext — credentials.rs::is_field_sensitive
- SSRF policy is a connector-metadata-gated exception, not a per-call decision

**Limits — when NOT to apply**

A hardened layer is only as good as its narrowest gate: exceptions (metadata-gated SSRF policy) must stay declarative and reviewable. Beware treating "in the trusted process" as sufficient — process-local does not mean unauthenticated is fine.

---
*Evidence counts are synthesis estimates over the 159-finding scan corpus (16 agents, two waves), not exact joins. Full per-finding evidence lives in the scan corpus; the divergences below carry verified file:line.*

### Deep-import the pure modules; keep the barrel off client paths _(proposed for this repo)_

A directory that mixes client-safe and server-only modules cannot be safely re-exported through one barrel: importing the barrel from a client path drags the database into the bundle. Deep-import the pure modules, ban value-imports of the barrel from client-reachable code, and apply a server-only marker at file level so accidental bundling fails the build instead of shipping.

CLAUDE.md: "Data seam: src/lib/data/ — signed-in users get REAL per-owner rows; anonymous/demo get the sample fixture. PURE modules (aggregates.ts, series.ts) are client-safe; everything else is server-only." and "Client-safety: never value-import @/lib/data (the barrel) or @/features/ledger (the UI barrel) from client-reachable code — deep-import the pure modules ... Use statement-form import type (inline { type X } leaves a side-effect import and drags the DB into the bundle)." This is a subtler rule than the feature-barrel rule (which requires barrel imports) — here the barrel is the thing to AVOID for a client path, showing the doctrine is context-sensitive rather than a blanket 'always use barrels'.

### Count forwarded-for hops from the right, and admit the limits _(proposed for this repo)_

An in-memory per-instance rate limiter is a first line against naive abuse, not a distributed guarantee — and it is worthless if the client key can be forged. Resolve the client address by counting a known number of trusted proxy hops from the right of the forwarded-for header rather than taking the leftmost entry, so padded forged hops cannot mint a fresh bucket per request, and state the limitation in the module rather than implying more.

`src/lib/rate-limit.ts:1-13` — "CAVEAT (documented, not hidden): this is PER-INSTANCE... this is a FIRST LINE that stops naive abuse, not a hard global guarantee." Lines 86-111 `clientIp()`: resolves from the right of `x-forwarded-for`, falling back to `x-real-ip` then a constant bucket key when the header has fewer entries than expected, "so unique-per-request spoofing can no longer mint a fresh rate-limit bucket each time."

### Gate an imported artifact in layers, one message per rejection _(proposed for this repo)_

Anything a user imports from another product — a workflow export, a config dump, model output — is untrusted input. Gate it in escalating layers: type, a hard byte cap, parse, a structural sniff, then per-element validators that drop corrupt items, with each rejection carrying its own specific message. Never let a partly-valid artifact reach application state.

The n8n/Zapier/Make/GitHub-Actions import path implements the ladder three times over, in three entry modes that share the same validators.

**File** — `sub_n8n/steps/upload/useFileUpload.ts`: `isSupportedFile(file.name)` → `file.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE` → read → empty check → for YAML a `jobs:` key sniff ("No 'jobs' key found. This does not appear to be a GitHub Actions workflow.") → `JSON.parse` → `countElements(json) === 0` → `detectPlatformLabel`. Each failure sets a distinct `{kind:'error', message}` preview.

**URL** — `sub_n8n/steps/upload/useUrlImport.ts` adds protocol allow-listing (`parsed.protocol !== 'https:' && !== 'http:'`), a fetch timeout (`AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)`), an HTTP status check and a post-fetch size cap, before running the same JSON/structure checks.

**Dispatch** — `sub_n8n/hooks/useWorkflowImport.ts` re-checks type and size against a **generated** limit shared with the backend (`MAX_WORKFLOW_JSON_BYTES` from `@/lib/n8nLimits.generated`), and wraps `parseWorkflowFile` in its own try/catch so a parser throw becomes a dispatched `SET_ERROR` rather than an unhandled rejection.

**Element-level** — `sub_n8n/hooks/n8nTypes.ts` `normalize

### Wipe a secret off the clipboard on a timer, forcibly if unsure _(proposed for this repo)_

A credential-grade payload placed on the OS clipboard stays there indefinitely, long after the flow that put it there is forgotten. Schedule an automatic clear after a short window: re-read first and clear only if your payload is still there, but if the read itself fails, wipe anyway — re-copying benign content is cheap, and an exfiltrated secret cannot be undone.

`src/features/settings/sub_network/components/BundleExportDialog.tsx` owns the whole policy in one helper:

```ts
const SENSITIVE_CLIPBOARD_TTL_MS = 30_000;

async function scheduleSensitiveClipboardClear(payload: string) {
  setTimeout(async () => {
    try {
      const current = await navigator.clipboard.readText();
      if (current === payload) await copyText('');
      // current !== payload: the user already copied something else. Leave it.
    } catch (readErr) {
      // Clipboard read failed (Tauri/Windows can deny on permission/focus).
      // A "skip wipe" branch would leave the secret in the OS clipboard
      // indefinitely -> force-wipe anyway.
      logger.warn('clipboard verify-before-wipe failed; force-wiping', { reason: readErr });
      await copyText('');
    }
  }, SENSITIVE_CLIPBOARD_TTL_MS);
}
```

Both secret-producing paths call it: `handleCopyToClipboard` (base64 bundle) and `handleCreateShareLink` (deep link). The comment names the trade-off explicitly — "the user can re-copy benign later content easily; an exfiltrated secret cannot be undone" — which is the reusable reasoning, not the 30s number.

### Gate a once-only secret reveal behind an acknowledgement _(proposed for this repo)_

When plaintext leaves the backend exactly once, every accidental exit from the dialog showing it is data loss. Remove backdrop-click dismissal, withhold the close affordance until an explicit acknowledgement, and make the confirm control visibly inert rather than merely non-functional until then.

`src/features/settings/sub_api_keys/components/CreatedKeyDialog.tsx`:

- The backdrop `motion.div` deliberately carries **no** `onClick={onClose}` — commented: *"No dismiss-on-backdrop-click — the user must explicitly acknowledge they've stored the plaintext, since this is the only time we'll show it."*
- The header `X` renders **only** `{acknowledged && ...}`.
- The Done button is `disabled={!acknowledged}` and additionally dimmed/scaled (`opacity-40 scale-[0.98]`) so the inert state is legible, not just non-functional.
- The same dialog also ships the token pre-substituted into a copyable MCP config block, so the user never has to re-derive the secret later.

The surrounding animation choices are documented as intentional weight-giving for an unrepeatable moment, all gated behind `useReducedMotion()`.

### Tag danger consent by which danger was shown, and bind the apply call to the exact preview it approved _(proposed for this repo)_

A single boolean 'user accepted the warning' lets consent for one hazard silently carry into a different hazard when server-derived flags flip between preview re-fetches. Tag the acknowledgement with the hazard kind, reset it whenever the preview's identity or trust fields change, and pass the previewed artifact's hash/preview id into the apply call so the thing imported is the thing that was reviewed.

`src/features/settings/sub_network/components/BundlePreviewContent.tsx` defines the discriminator and the reasoning:

```ts
/** 'tamper' -> trusted peer with a bad signature; 'unknown' -> unverifiable signer. */
export type DangerConfirmKind = 'tamper' | 'unknown' | null;
// signer_trusted is server-derived and can flip between preview re-fetches.
// A single shared boolean previously let consent for warning A carry into warning B.
```

`BundleImportDialog.tsx` enforces it at both ends:

```ts
useEffect(() => { setDangerConfirmed(null); },
  [preview?.bundle_hash, preview?.signer_trusted, preview?.signature_valid]);
...
const requiredKind = preview.signer_trusted ? 'tamper' : 'unknown';
const matchedKind = dangerConfirmed === requiredKind;   // gates "Import anyway"
```

and closes the TOCTOU window on apply:

```ts
const options = {
  skip_conflicts, rename_prefix,
  preview_id: preview?.preview_id ?? null,
  expected_bundle_hash: preview?.bundle_hash ?? null,
};
```

### Disarm the approve button for a beat whenever a queued consent request is replaced _(proposed for this repo)_

Modals that surface a queue of consequential requests (run remote code, grant an origin access) must re-disarm their primary action every time the head of the queue changes, so a click already in flight against the previous item cannot auto-approve its replacement.

Two independent root-mounted gates converged on the same guard.

`src/features/cloud/RemoteApprovalPrompt.tsx`:

```ts
const APPROVE_ARM_DELAY_MS = 450; // approving runs remote code locally
const currentId = current?.id;
useEffect(() => {
  setArmed(false);
  const tid = setTimeout(() => setArmed(true), APPROVE_ARM_DELAY_MS);
  return () => clearTimeout(tid);
}, [currentId]);
// <Button ... disabled={!armed}>
```

`src/features/settings/sub_api_keys/components/PairApprovalModal.tsx` repeats it keyed on `nonce`, and in the same per-request reset also re-defaults the scope selection to exactly what was requested. Note the shape: the delay is keyed on request identity, not on mount — the hazard is queue advancement, not first paint.

### Hand the renderer a session ref, redeem the token server-side _(proposed for this repo)_

When an interactive flow mints secret material in the backend, returning it to the UI so the UI can send it back on save moves the secret across the process boundary twice for no reason. Return an opaque session reference instead, hold the tokens encrypted server-side, and redeem the reference inside the privileged save command — stripping the transport-only key so it can never be persisted as a field.

The renderer's OAuth hook builds its credential payload from a *reference*, explicitly dropping `client_id` / `client_secret` and never touching token material:

`src/features/vault/shared/hooks/useCredentialOAuth.ts`
```ts
const { client_id: _cid, client_secret: _csec, ...safePendingValues } = pv;
const credentialData = {
  ...safePendingValues,
  // The backend redeems the ref into the real refresh token at save /
  // preview-healthcheck time — no token material in the renderer.
  [OAUTH_FIELD.SESSION_REF]: data.oauth_session_ref,
  ...
};
```
The pending values (which may still contain a `client_secret` en route to consent) are held in a `useRef`, not state — the comment says why: *"to avoid exposure via React DevTools, Sentry, and error boundary serialization."*

## testing

### Keep business logic pure and inject the provider seam _(proposed for this repo)_

Logic that hard-imports an LLM client or a database can only be tested by mocking modules, which couples the suite to the wiring rather than the behaviour. Write the logic as pure functions over plain data, taking any external capability as an injected interface so production passes the real one and tests pass a fake function. Where the behaviour under test is the query itself, use a real in-memory database rather than a mock query layer, so the SQL stays covered.

`src/lib/ai/ledger-agent.ts:20-21`: "The LLM seam is INJECTED ... rather than hard-imported, so this module stays pure + unit-testable without server-only: /api/ask passes the real @/lib/ai generateText, tests pass a fake." `src/services/ledger.test.ts` header: "Pure module — no Gemini, no env, no I/O." CLAUDE.md: "DB-backed tests use the memory:// PGlite harness (see ledger.test.ts header)." Test runner is plain node:test via tsx, not Jest/Vitest — a deliberately thin toolchain choice (package.json `test` script).

### Gate evals on curated fixtures: hard zero-tolerance, soft baselines _(proposed for this repo)_

An evaluation harness that only reports scores never blocks anything, and one that hard-gates every metric blocks on noise. Seed hand-curated gold fixtures per concern and run the real stage code against them, standing in an oracle only for the genuinely non-deterministic judgement. Split the gates: correctness and safety properties are unconditional zero-tolerance, while quality metrics compare against a committed baseline with a bounded regression tolerance that must be recalibrated deliberately, never silently.

`crates/brainiac-eval/src/lib.rs:1-23` — five profiles enumerated with what each isolates. `crates/brainiac-eval/src/gates.rs:1-36` — hard vs soft gate split, per-metric delta constants, and a `default_reranker` back-compat shim so pre-reranker baselines stay valid. Baselines committed at `results/baseline.json`, `results/contradiction-baseline.json`, `results/divergence-baseline.json`, etc.

### Run one storage suite against every driver, real or faked _(proposed for this repo)_

Two storage drivers behind one interface typecheck identically and behave differently, and the differences are exactly the semantics the type signature cannot express — create-if-absent, partial merge, transactional idempotency. Write the storage tests against the interface and execute the same suite against every driver, faking the one you cannot run locally. The bugs this catches are silent data loss, not error messages.

`src/lib/db/store.ts:404-407` documents a parity bug this caught: createReport must be "create-if-absent: a duplicate id is a no-op that returns the EXISTING report ... never a throw (PGlite) or a destructive clobber (Firestore) — both were parity bugs (a re-create blanked a populated report)." Test files per store surface: `analysis-store.test.ts`, `certificate-store.test.ts`, `credit-store.test.ts`, `fact-ledger-store.test.ts`, `firestore-store.money.test.ts`, `grants-store.test.ts`, `reminder-store.test.ts`, `research-store.test.ts` sit alongside `__tests__/firestore-fake.ts`. Repo-wide there are ~201 `*.test.ts(x)` files.

### Guard server-only modules at runtime and inject their deps lazily _(proposed for this repo)_

Marking a module server-only with a build-time package makes it unresolvable to lightweight test runners, so the modules that most need protection become the ones with no unit tests. Use a tiny runtime assertion instead, and have each module reach its real infrastructure through a lazily-imported defaults function passed as an optional last parameter. The same module is then both the production wiring and a pure, injectable unit with no mocking framework — and re-reading config per call keeps a rotated key effective without a restart.

`src/lib/serverOnlyGuard.ts:1-15` is the single 15-line primitive: throws if `window !== undefined`. Reused identically in `src/lib/auth/authorizeRoute.ts:6-7`, `src/lib/tokens/guard.ts:5-6`, and (per its own docstring) `@/lib/auth/session`. The DI convention repeats verbatim in `authorizeRoute.ts` (`AuthzDeps`/`defaultDeps`), `operation.ts` (`AiOperationDeps`/`defaultDeps()`, explicitly cross-referencing the rate-limit.ts precedent), and `tokens/guard.ts` (`GuardDeps`/`defaultDeps()`) — each caches its wired defaults once per process but re-reads env/config per call so a rotated key or toggled flag takes effect without a restart (documented explicitly in `operation.ts:225-236`).

### Layer the test surface by what only that layer can catch _(proposed for this repo)_

A single test tier always over-serves one risk and misses another, so decide the layers deliberately rather than accumulating them. Fast unit tests cover pure logic and constrain the runner choice (pick one that can import your server-guarded modules), browser-driven suites cover journeys, and separate configurations keep functional checks apart from user-acceptance journeys. Model-dependent behaviour needs its own evaluation lane, because a pass/fail assertion is the wrong instrument for output quality.

package.json scripts: `test` = `tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`, `e2e` = `playwright test`, `uat` = `playwright test -c playwright.uat.config.ts`, `eval:llm` = `tsx scripts/llm-eval/run.ts`. `e2e/engine.ts` + `e2e/llm-routes.api.spec.ts` + `e2e/qualify-draft.ui.spec.ts` exist alongside a `.pglite` sqlite-analog datadir checked into `e2e/uat/` (looks like a committed local DB snapshot for reproducible e2e runs — worth checking that's intentional, not accidental commit noise). `tiger/` mirrors the cross-project /tiger skill's call-site + character + session structure.

### Extract framework-free predicates out of middleware plumbing _(proposed for this repo)_

Gating decisions written inside framework middleware can only be tested by booting the framework's runtime, so in practice they are not tested at all. Extract the decision into a pure predicate over a small explicit input type with no framework imports, and reduce the middleware to request and response plumbing that calls it. Ordering the rules explicitly in that predicate is what makes fail-open and fail-closed cases reviewable.

`src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:1-46` — "extracted from middleware.ts so the presence-gate decision and the protected-prefix predicate are unit-testable without next/server." `decideRoute()` explicit rule ordering: dev-auth always passes, keyless (no provider) always passes, only a live firebase provider + protected path + missing session cookie redirects.

### Measure coverage on logic layers and ratchet the floor _(proposed for this repo)_

A repo-wide coverage percentage measures mostly presentational code and turns the gate into a number nobody trusts. Scope the measurement to the logic core — libraries, feature logic, route handlers — excluding presentational components, barrels and vendored code, so the figure means something. Then pin the thresholds just under the current measured value so the gate blocks a regression without demanding a coverage big-bang, and raise them as real work lands.

`vitest.config.ts:28-56`: comment states the stance directly — 'Measure the LOGIC core... not presentational .tsx pages/components... per the test-mastery scan's "coverage that matters" stance' and 'thresholds are pinned just UNDER the measured baseline so the gate blocks a REGRESSION... without demanding a big-bang backfill.' Baseline noted as having moved 53.85% → 77.72% lines across waves T1-T5, with thresholds at lines 77 / statements 77 / functions 83 / branches 84. 113 test files under `tests/`, plus a separate Playwright `e2e/` suite driving named UAT-style journey specs (uat-10-visitor.spec.ts … uat-80-reference.spec.ts).

### Test against a real migrated database and control time by writing it _(proposed for this repo)_

A mocked store drifts from the real schema, and tests that sleep to exercise aging or expiry logic are slow and flaky. Spin a fresh temp-directory database per test through the full migration chain, so the migrations themselves stay covered, and make time deterministic by writing explicit timestamps into rows rather than waiting for the clock. One integration file per storage-backed subsystem keeps the failures legible.

`crates/core/tests/jobs.rs:1-4` module doc: "Timestamps are manipulated directly so the tests are deterministic (no sleeping)." `fresh_db` (lines 13-22) builds a `StorageConfig` pointing at `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("pumper-{tag}-{}", Uuid::new_v4()))` and calls `Storage::connect(&cfg).await.expect("connect + migrate")`. `insert_queued` (lines 26-40) computes `created = Utc::now() - Duration::seconds(waited_secs)` and inserts it directly via raw `sqlx::query`, side-stepping the need to actually wait real wall-clock time to test aging/starvation logic. Five more integration-test files (`cache.rs`, `datasets.rs`, `tiers.rs`, `triggers.rs`, `webhook_deliveries.rs`) sit alongside, one per storage-backed subsystem.

### A multi-driver store needs a parity suite, not a shared interface _(proposed for this repo)_

A shared storage interface makes every driver typecheck, which is exactly why teams stop there and ship divergent semantics. The interface cannot express create-if-absent, partial merge, or transactional idempotency, so those differences surface only as data loss in whichever environment runs the weaker driver. Treat cross-driver execution of the same suite as a required tier whenever more than one driver exists, however thin the second one is.

**Why this is one shared problem**

Five members independently chose the same pluggable-Store architecture, so they inherit the same risk: two drivers that typecheck identically and behave differently. Grant Writing Nonprofits proved the risk is real (a duplicate-id create silently clobbering data, caught only by running the suite twice); the others rely on interface-level intent or logic-layer coverage that cannot catch it.

**Current approaches**

- **Grant Writing Nonprofits** — Storage tests are written against the Store interface and run against both the PGlite driver and a hand-rolled Firestore fake, catching parity bugs such as a duplicate-id create silently clobbering data.
- **Medical Bill Negotiator** — Pushes idempotency and lifecycle-guard invariants into the Store contract so every driver (pg/pglite/sqlite) is forced to honor them, but coverage thresholds are scoped to logic layers only — no cross-driver execution.
- **Immigration Paperwork** — One Store interface with Firestore in prod and PGlite locally chosen by dbDriver(); the multi-tier test surface (tsx --test, Playwright, LLM eval) has no driver-parity tier.
- **Local SEO Agency** — Enforces the persis

### Write policy decisions as pure functions over plain data _(proposed for this repo)_

Policy — route gating, provider ordering, access scope, output quality — is the part of a system most worth testing and the part most often entangled with I/O and SDK imports. Express each decision as a dependency-free function over plain data with the clock and any config passed in, and keep the framework and network calls strictly outside it. Independently converged on by several projects in this portfolio, which makes it a candidate workspace-wide default rather than a local preference.

**Independently converged on by 5 projects**

- Local SEO Agency
- Grant Writing Nonprofits
- ai-bookkeeper
- Immigration Paperwork
- brainiac

A pattern this many projects reached independently is a candidate workspace-wide standard.

### Move a component's computation into a React-free sibling module _(proposed for this repo)_

When the interesting part of a component is a computation — bucketing, faceting, scoring, smoothing, reachability — testing it through the component means booting a DOM to assert arithmetic. Put the computation in a plain module beside the component, generic over the row type via injected accessors so it knows nothing about the feature's shapes, and unit-test it directly while the component keeps only rendering. The payoff is what becomes cheap to assert: hysteresis bands, deep facet trees, gating rules.

Four instances in this scope, each with the rationale in its header comment and a matching test:

- `display/grouping.ts` — *"Intentionally React-free so the bucketing logic is unit-testable in isolation."* (`__tests__/grouping.test.ts`)
- `display/facetedTableModel.ts` — *"React-free on purpose — the rendering side lives in FacetedDecisionTable."* Generic: *"every domain hook is an injected accessor (`getGroupPath`, `haystack`), so nothing here knows about knowledge items, ideas, or any other feature shape."* (`__tests__/facetedTableModel.test.ts`)
- `layout/systemLoad.ts` — *"all the UX tuning (smoothing + the green/amber/red banding) lives here so it is cheap to iterate and unit-testable without a DOM."* (`layout/systemLoad.test.ts`)
- `chrome/commandPaletteUtils.ts` — *"Keeping this pure (no React, no stores) makes the palette's reachability contract unit-testable."* (`chrome/commandPaletteUtils.test.ts`); `chrome/fleetStripModel.ts` + `fleetStripModel.test.ts` is the same split for the activity strip.
